name: bfq_bfqq_expire
prose: Precondition: bfqd is the bfq_data whose in-service queue is bfqq, compensate says whether to compensate for idle-time overestimation, reason is a valid expiration cause, and the caller holds the bfq_data lock. Postcondition: the function returns nothing. It computes slow with bfq_bfqq_is_slow(bfqd, bfqq, compensate, &delta); delta starts at 0 and is overwritten (in milliseconds of service time) only when bfqq is a sync queue, otherwise slow is false and delta stays 0. If bfqq->wr_coeff == 1 and (slow, or reason == BFQQE_BUDGET_TIMEOUT with budget left >= entity->budget / 3), the queue is charged delta (time) instead of service via bfq_bfqq_charge_time. If bfqd->low_latency and wr_coeff == 1, last_wr_start_finish is set to jiffies. If bfqd->low_latency, bfqd->bfq_wr_max_softrt_rate > 0 and bfqq->sort_list is empty: soft_rt_next_start is recomputed with bfq_bfqq_softrt_next_start when bfqq->dispatched == 0, else if dispatched > 0 the softrt_update flag is marked. bfqd->rqs_injected and bfqd->wait_dispatch are set to false and bfqd->waited_rq to NULL. The budget is recomputed with __bfq_bfqq_recalc_budget(bfqd, bfqq, reason) and the queue expired with __bfq_bfqq_expire; if that returns true (bfqq gone) the function returns at once without touching any service counter. Otherwise: if bfqq is not busy and reason is neither BFQQE_BUDGET_TIMEOUT nor BFQQE_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED the queue is marked non_blocking_wait_rq and bfqq->entity.service is kept, else bfqq->entity.service is set to 0; in both cases the service field of every parent entity (entity->parent, then upward through for_each_entity: all ancestors with CONFIG_BFQ_GROUP_IOSCHED, a single level otherwise) is then set to 0. No lock or reference is acquired or released by this function itself.
note: bfq-iosched.c:4431-4450 the code ends with entity = entity->parent; for_each_entity(entity) entity->service = 0; (parent counters ARE reset). Prose tightened: delta stays 0 for non-sync queue (4156), ancestors via for_each_entity (bfq-iosched.h:1105,1123).

name: venus_statfs
prose: Precondition: dentry is a valid dentry of a coda superblock and sfs points to writable struct kstatfs storage. Postcondition: it allocates a zeroed upcall buffer (kvzalloc); if that fails it returns -ENOMEM at once (no upcall is sent, sfs unchanged). Otherwise it performs a synchronous CODA_STATFS upcall to Venus via coda_upcall on the superblock's channel; if that returns 0 it sets sfs->f_blocks, f_bfree, f_bavail, f_files and f_ffree from Venus's reply and returns 0; if it returns an error (for example -ENXIO when Venus is not running, -ENOMEM when coda_upcall cannot allocate, -EINTR when interrupted, or the negated Venus result) that error is returned and sfs is left unchanged. Once the buffer was allocated it is always freed with kvfree before returning; the function takes no locks of its own and keeps no references.
note: upcall.c:61-67 UPARG returns PTR_ERR(-ENOMEM) from kvzalloc (45-51); statfs fields set only if !error (upcall.c venus_statfs); kvfree(inp) always. Only wording of -ENOMEM sources made non-exhaustive.

name: changed_inode
prose: Precondition: sctx is an initialized send context whose cmp_key identifies the inode, left_path/right_path point at the inode items needed for result (NEW and CHANGED use left_path, DELETED and CHANGED use right_path), and result is a btrfs_compare_tree_result. Postcondition: first it closes the previous current inode (drops its page cache range if requested and iput) and resets cur_ino = cmp_key->objectid, cur_inode_new_gen = false, cur_inode_last_extent = (u64)-1, cur_inode_next_write_offset = 0, ignore_cur_inode = false, empties cur_inode_path and sets send_progress = cur_ino. Then for NEW: if the inode has nlink 0 it sets ignore_cur_inode and returns 0; otherwise it fills cur_inode_gen/new/deleted/size/mode/rdev from the send tree and, unless it is the root directory, calls send_create_inode_if_needed. For DELETED it fills gen, size and mode from the parent tree, marks the inode deleted and not new, and returns 0. For CHANGED: if both nlinks are 0 it ignores the inode and returns 0; cur_inode_new_gen is set when the generations differ (not for the root directory) or exactly one nlink is 0; in the new_gen case it processes the old inode as deleted (process_all_refs DELETED) when the old nlink is > 0, then, if the new nlink is > 0, as a new inode (send_create_inode_if_needed, process_all_refs NEW, send_progress = cur_ino + 1, process_all_extents, process_all_new_xattrs); otherwise it records the send-tree gen, size and mode with new and deleted false. Returns 0, or the negative errno of the first failing step, in which case the per-inode fields may be only partly updated.
note: send.c:6770-6941 changed_inode ends at out: return ret (no trim_dir_utimes_cache; that is in finish_inode_if_needed, 6680-6740 area). NEW nlink0 and DELETED paths leave ret=0. send_create_inode_if_needed returns <=0.

name: ceph_lock
prose: Real function name is ceph_lock(file, cmd, fl) (the packet name ceph_fcntl does not exist in the source; the slice cuts the head of ceph_lock, so the name is absent from the slice). Precondition: file is an open ceph file, fl a valid file_lock, cmd an fcntl lock command (F_GETLK, F_SETLK or F_SETLKW style); the caller holds no ceph locks. Postcondition: it returns -ENOLCK if FL_POSIX is not set in fl->c.flc_flags and -ESTALE if the inode is shut down, in both cases with no side effects. The operation is GETFILELOCK for F_GETLK and SETFILELOCK otherwise, and a local wait flag is set for F_SETLKW (also when the lock is an unlock). While holding ci->i_ceph_lock briefly it reads CEPH_I_ERROR_FILELOCK; if set it returns -EIO (before that, for a SETFILELOCK-type unlock it calls posix_lock_file(file, fl, NULL) to drop the local lock and ignores its result). For a SETFILELOCK unlock it then calls try_unlock_file, which temporarily adds FL_EXISTS and calls locks_lock_file_wait: only when that returns -ENOENT does ceph_lock return early (0 if the caller had not set FL_EXISTS, -ENOENT if it had) and nothing is sent to the MDS; for any other local result, success or another error, try_unlock_file returns 1 and the function continues. It then calls ceph_lock_message (CEPH_LOCK_FCNTL, the lock type derived from fl as shared, exclusive or unlock); that function forces wait to 0 for unlock requests and for GETFILELOCK, so the MDS request waits only for a non-unlock SETLKW. For SETFILELOCK ceph_lock_message first sets fl->fl_ops to the ceph lock ops and increments i_filelock_ref and takes an inode reference (igrab) through fl_copy_lock (both released later by fl_release_private), whether or not the request then fails. If ceph_lock_message fails its negative error is returned. If it succeeds for GETLK, 0 is returned with fl filled in from the MDS reply; if it succeeds for a SETFILELOCK whose fl->c.flc_type is not F_UNLCK, the lock is also applied locally with posix_lock_file: if that fails a CEPH_LOCK_UNLOCK ceph_lock_message is sent to undo the remote lock (its result ignored) and the posix_lock_file error is returned; otherwise 0 is returned.
note: locks.c ceph_lock: wait=1 for IS_SETLKW irrespective of unlock but ceph_lock_message forces wait=0 for unlock/non-SETFILELOCK (locks.c:93-95); try_unlock_file (231-244) returns err only for -ENOENT, else 1 so other local errors do NOT return early

name: afs_create_yfs_cm_token
prose: Real function afs_create_yfs_cm_token(challenge, server) in fs/afs/cm_security.c (slice cuts the head). Precondition: server is a valid afs_server whose cell->net is valid; challenge is the received rxrpc challenge skb. Postcondition: returns -ENOKEY if net->fs_cm_token_key is NULL and -ENOPKG if no krb5 enctype matches rxgk_kernel_query_challenge(challenge), in both cases before anything is allocated; -ENOMEM if the appdata buffer allocation (kzalloc) fails; the negative error PTR_ERR(aead) if crypto_krb5_prepare_encryption fails (in that case there is no aead handle to free and only the appdata buffer is kfree'd); or the negative error from crypto_krb5_encrypt (in that case the aead handle is freed and the appdata buffer is kfree'd). Otherwise it builds the XDR appdata (initiator and acceptor UUIDs, capability list, connection enctype, a fresh random callback key K0, and a token container whose encrypted token holds K0, level ENCRYPT, zero times and one identity with the server UUID), encrypts the token in place, stores adatasize and the appdata pointer into server->cm_rxgk_appdata (overwriting its previous value without freeing it; ownership of the buffer passes to the server), frees the aead handle and returns the non-negative result of crypto_krb5_encrypt (the size of the secured blob, not necessarily 0). On every failure path server->cm_rxgk_appdata is left unchanged. A size mismatch between the built layout and adatasize only logs pr_err and does not abort.
note: cm_security.c:325-340 and head 178-205: IS_ERR(aead) goes to out_token (no aead to free); crypto_krb5_encrypt returns blob size (krb5_api.c:365)

name: btrfs_recover_relocation
prose: Precondition: called while mounting a read-write btrfs filesystem to resume a relocation interrupted by a crash; fs_info->tree_root and fs_info->data_reloc_root are usable. Postcondition: it allocates a path (-ENOMEM at once on failure) and scans the tree root backwards from key (BTRFS_TREE_RELOC_OBJECTID, ROOT_ITEM, (u64)-1) for ROOT_ITEMs with objectid BTRFS_TREE_RELOC_OBJECTID, reading each with btrfs_read_tree_root and collecting it; for a reloc root with root refs > 0 whose fs root lookup fails with -ENOENT it zeroes the reloc root's refs via mark_garbage_root (any other lookup error aborts). If the search lands before the first item of the tree root (slot 0 after a failed exact search) the scan stops with ret still 1. If no reloc roots were collected it skips the recovery. Otherwise it allocates a reloc control (-ENOMEM on failure), starts a reloc chunk (reloc_chunk_start), joins a transaction on the extent root, and for each collected reloc root: roots whose refs are 0 are only queued on rc->reloc_roots; for the others it looks up the fs root (any error, including -ENOENT, aborts and ends the transaction), registers the reloc root with __add_reloc_root and attaches it to the fs root. It then commits that transaction, merges the reloc roots with their fs roots (merge_reloc_roots), joins and commits another transaction, and cleans dirty subvolumes (clean_dirty_subvols; its error is reported only if no earlier error occurred). On every path after the path allocation it frees the not yet processed reloc roots list and the path, and frees the reloc control if allocated; it ends the reloc chunk if reloc_chunk_start succeeded and releases the recovered fs roots on the paths taken after the transaction-joining loop has started. Finally, if ret == 0 it runs btrfs_orphan_cleanup on the data relocation root (reference grabbed and put) and returns its result; this includes the case where no reloc roots were found. Returns 0 on success, a negative errno from the failing step (-ENOMEM, btrfs_search_slot, btrfs_read_tree_root, btrfs_get_fs_root, mark_garbage_root, reloc_chunk_start, joining or committing a transaction, __add_reloc_root, clean_dirty_subvols, or btrfs_orphan_cleanup), or the positive value 1 in the corner case above where the search stopped at slot 0 and the reloc roots list was empty (in that case the orphan cleanup is skipped).
note: relocation.c:4115-4130: ret>0 with slots[0]==0 breaks with ret=1, empty list goes to out and returns 1 (ret==0 test skipped); second loop btrfs_get_fs_root error aborts incl. -ENOENT

name: ceph_check_caps
prose: Precondition: ci is a valid inode info, the caller holds an inode reference and does NOT hold ci->i_ceph_lock; flags is a combination of CHECK_CAPS_* bits. The function takes no session argument and holds no session reference on entry. Postcondition: returns void with ci->i_ceph_lock released and any session reference it took internally dropped (every iteration puts the previously held session, and the final put releases the last one). If CEPH_I_ASYNC_CREATE is set it sets CEPH_I_ASYNC_CHECK_CAPS, releases the lock and returns immediately without reconciling caps or sending any message (no session reference is held at that point). Otherwise it adds CHECK_CAPS_FLUSH if CEPH_I_FLUSH is set and CHECK_CAPS_FLUSH_FORCE if CEPH_I_FLUSH_FORCE is set, computes wanted/used/retain caps, may try a non-blocking invalidate of cached pages (queuing an invalidate if it fails), then scans ci->i_caps in increasing mds order (skipping non-auth caps with CHECK_CAPS_AUTHONLY): for any cap needing action (completed revocation, forced flush, new max_size requested, size reporting, dirty caps to flush, snap flush pending, wanted caps change, or issued caps beyond retain) it takes a reference on that cap's session, first kicking flushing caps and flushing snaps and restarting the scan if the auth cap has CEPH_I_KICK_FLUSH or CEPH_I_FLUSH_SNAPS set, otherwise marks dirty caps flushing, drops i_ceph_lock, sends an update cap message via __send_cap, retakes the lock and restarts the scan. When no more caps need messages it may requeue the inode on the delayed-cap list, releases the lock, drops the session reference, and queues writeback (if a Fb revoke is blocked by wrbuffer refs) and/or invalidation if flagged.
note: caps.c:2033 void ceph_check_caps(struct ceph_inode_info *ci, int flags): no session argument; local session starts NULL (2048) and is put at 2302; ack: puts previous and gets cap->session (2204-2205)

name: affs_readdir
prose: Precondition: file is an open AFFS directory whose private_data points to a valid struct affs_dir_data (allocated by affs_dir_open); ctx->pos is 0 or 1 for the start, or encodes the resume position as ((hash_pos << 16) | chain_pos) + 2; the caller holds the usual directory read serialisation (inode lock shared); may sleep. Postcondition: if ctx->pos < 2 it sets data->ino to 0 and emits "." and ".." with dir_emit_dots, returning 0 immediately (before taking the directory lock, without updating data->cookie) if that emit fails. It then takes the AFFS directory lock, which is released before return on every path after that. A chain_pos of 0xffff logs a warning and moves ctx->pos to the start of the next hash bucket. If the directory header block cannot be read it returns 0 at once (after unlocking) without emitting and without changing data->cookie or data->ino. If data->ino is non-zero and the directory inode version equals data->cookie it resumes directly at block data->ino; otherwise it walks chain_pos entries of the chain of bucket hash_pos; a failed block read during this walk is logged, the directory header buffer is released and the function returns -EIO, again without updating data->cookie or data->ino. If the chain has fewer entries it continues with the following non-empty hash buckets, setting ctx->pos to the start of each new bucket. Entries are emitted with dir_emit(name, namelen, block number, DT_UNKNOWN) and ctx->pos is incremented per emitted entry; if dir_emit returns false the emission stops. A failed read of an entry block while emitting is logged and only ends the current chain (emission continues with the next non-empty bucket). When emission ends normally or by a dir_emit refusal, data->cookie is set to the current inode version and data->ino to the current chain variable ino: the block number of the entry that was refused (0 when everything was emitted; after an unreadable entry block it is that block's number unless a later non-empty bucket was completed). All buffer heads are released. The return value is 0, or -EIO only for the failed block read while skipping to the resume position in the chain.
note: dir.c:104-106 header-read failure goes to out_unlock_dir (no cookie/ino update); dir.c:119-124 -EIO goes to out_brelse_dir; cookie/ino only set at done: (dir.c:156-158)

name: load_elf_fdpic_binary
prose: Real function load_elf_fdpic_binary(bprm) in fs/binfmt_elf_fdpic.c (the slice starts in the middle of its program-header scan, so the name is not in the slice). Precondition: bprm is a linux_binprm whose buf holds the ELF header read from bprm->file; called from exec in process context. Postcondition: returns 0 after the FDPIC image is loaded and started (begin_new_exec has flushed the old image, the executable and interpreter are mapped with elf_fdpic_map_file, the stack, brk and auxiliary tables are set up, and start_thread has initialised the user registers), after the interpreter file reference (if any) has been dropped with fput. Returns a negative errno on failure: -ENOEXEC if the header is not a valid ELF (is_elf), or is not FDPIC on an MMU build (on a non-MMU build, not FDPIC and not ET_DYN), or if kernel_read of the PT_INTERP name or of the interpreter header returns a short NON-NEGATIVE count (a negative kernel_read result is returned unchanged, not converted to -ENOEXEC); -ENOMEM if a PT_INTERP segment is longer than PATH_MAX; -ENOENT if a PT_INTERP segment is shorter than 2 bytes, if the allocation of the interpreter name (kmalloc) fails (retval is -ENOENT at that point, not -ENOMEM), or if the name has no terminating NUL; the PTR_ERR of open_exec for the interpreter; -ELIBBAD if the interpreter is not a valid ELF; or the error propagated from elf_fdpic_fetch_phdrs (for either file), begin_new_exec, setup_arg_pages and arch_setup_additional_pages (MMU), elf_fdpic_map_file, vm_mmap (non-MMU) or create_elf_fdpic_tables. Only the first PT_INTERP header is used. Every return path goes through one exit that kfrees interpreter_name, exec_params.phdrs, exec_params.loadmap, interp_params.phdrs and interp_params.loadmap (the loadmaps have been copied to the user stack by then) and, if the interpreter file is still held, allows write access to it and fputs it; mappings made after begin_new_exec are not unmapped here.
note: binfmt_elf_fdpic.c: interpreter header read: if (retval >= 0) retval = -ENOEXEC; negative propagated (slice 297-300, same pattern for the name read at ~257); kmalloc failure goto error with retval=-ENOENT (~253-255)

name: sb_write_pointer
prose: Precondition: bdev is the block device, zones points to the two (BTRFS_NR_SB_LOG_ZONES) superblock log zone descriptors of one mirror, neither of which is a conventional zone (asserted), and wp_ret points to a writable u64. A zone counts as empty when its condition is BLK_ZONE_COND_EMPTY, and as full when its condition is BLK_ZONE_COND_FULL or its write pointer plus one superblock (SUPER_INFO_SECTORS) would exceed start + capacity. Postcondition: the states are tested in this order. (1) Both zones empty: *wp_ret is set to the byte address of the start of zones[0] and -ENOENT is returned (no superblock written yet). (2) Both zones full: it reads the last superblock slot of each zone through the block device page cache (the invalidate lock is held only around each read; an error from read_cache_page_gfp is returned, after releasing the first superblock page if the second read failed, and *wp_ret is not written) and sets *wp_ret to the byte address of the start of zones[1] if the generation of the superblock in zones[0] is greater than that in zones[1], otherwise of zones[0], then releases both superblock pages and returns 0. (3) Otherwise, if zone 0 is not full and zone 1 is empty or full (that is, zone 0 empty or partly written with zone 1 empty or full, or zone 0 empty with zone 1 full): *wp_ret is the byte address of the write pointer of zones[0] and 0 is returned. (4) Otherwise, if zone 0 is full (zone 1 then is not full, whether empty or partly written): *wp_ret is the byte address of the write pointer of zones[1] and 0 is returned. (5) In every remaining state (zone 0 not full and zone 1 partly written, i.e. neither empty nor full) it returns -EUCLEAN without writing *wp_ret. No reference or lock stays held.
note: zoned.c sb_write_pointer: chain is if(!full[0] && (empty[1]||full[1])) zones[0].wp; else if(full[0]) zones[1].wp; else -EUCLEAN, so full[0] with empty[1] returns zones[1].wp and 0

name: dlm_midcomms_close
prose: Precondition: nodeid is any integer node id; the caller holds neither close_lock nor nodes_srcu (the function calls synchronize_srcu(&nodes_srcu), which would deadlock inside a read-side section, and takes close_lock, a mutex that is not recursive) and may sleep. Postcondition: it always performs these steps in order: (1) under an SRCU read lock it looks the node up and, only if one exists, sets DLM_NODE_FLAG_CLOSE on it and wakes its shutdown_wait waiters; (2) it waits for an SRCU grace period with synchronize_srcu (also when no node was found); (3) it takes close_lock and looks the node up again under a new SRCU read lock. If the second lookup finds no node (whether or not the first did), it releases the SRCU read lock and close_lock and returns the value of dlm_lowcomms_close(nodeid) (0 on success or a negative errno), having done nothing else to midcomms state. If the second lookup finds a node, it calls dlm_lowcomms_close(nodeid) and remembers its value, deletes the node's debugfs comms file, unlinks the node from the node hash under nodes_lock (hlist_del_rcu), releases the SRCU read lock, waits for another SRCU grace period so no reader remains, drops all pending messages with dlm_send_queue_flush(node), schedules the node to be freed with call_srcu(midcomms_node_release), releases close_lock and returns the remembered value of dlm_lowcomms_close; the caller must not use the node afterwards. close_lock and the SRCU read lock are released on every path before returning.
note: midcomms.c dlm_midcomms_close: synchronize_srcu and mutex_lock(close_lock) run before the second nodeid2node, so the no-node path (even with no node at the first lookup) does take close_lock and wait for a grace period; node-exists path same as before

name: EXT4_FEATURE_COMPAT_FUNCS(journal,		HAS_JOURNAL)

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE3(io_submit, aio_context_t, ctx_id, long, nr,
prose: Generated syscall sys_io_submit(ctx_id, nr, iocbpp). Precondition: iocbpp is a user pointer to an array of nr user iocb pointers. Postcondition: returns -EINVAL if nr < 0 or lookup_ioctx(ctx_id) finds no context. Otherwise it clamps nr to ctx->nr_events, brackets the loop with blk_start_plug/blk_finish_plug when nr > AIO_PLUG_THRESHOLD, and submits the iocbs one at a time with io_submit_one(ctx, user_iocb, false) until one fails. Stopping at index i (0 <= i <= nr, i being the number submitted successfully), it returns i if i > 0, otherwise the first error: -EFAULT if the iocb pointer could not be read from user memory, or the error of io_submit_one (e.g. -EFAULT, -EINVAL, -EAGAIN, -EBADF, or a handler error), or 0 if nothing was attempted (nr == 0 after clamping). The context reference from lookup_ioctx is dropped before returning on every path after the lookup.
note: aio.c SYSCALL_DEFINE3(io_submit): nr<0 -> -EINVAL; lookup_ioctx; clamp to nr_events; plug if > AIO_PLUG_THRESHOLD; return i ? i : ret; percpu_ref_put(&ctx->users) on all paths after lookup

name: emit_fiemap_extent
prose: Precondition: fieinfo, cache (holding at most one cached extent when cache->cached is true, plus the entries[] array of size entries_size and the counters entries_pos, extents_mapped), and a new extent (offset, phys, len, flags) not carrying FIEMAP_EXTENT_LAST (asserted); the extents are presented in increasing offset order, possibly overlapping the cached one after a re-search. Postcondition: it merges, replaces, trims or stores the new extent against the cached one and returns 0, 1 or BTRFS_FIEMAP_FLUSH_CACHE (a negative value below -MAX_ERRNO). If nothing is cached, the cache is replaced by the new extent and 0 returned. Otherwise, if the cached extent ends after the new offset (cache->offset + cache->len > offset): if offset equals cache->offset the cache is simply replaced by the new extent (0 returned); if offset is greater than cache->offset the cached length is cut to offset - cache->offset and the cached extent is then stored (see below); if offset is less than cache->offset the new extent is ignored (0 returned, cache unchanged) when it ends at or before the cached end, otherwise its part past the cached end is kept (offset moved to the cached end, len reduced, phys advanced by the same amount unless the flags include FIEMAP_EXTENT_ENCODED or FIEMAP_EXTENT_DELALLOC) and the cached extent is stored. If the cached extent does not end after offset and the new extent is contiguous in logical and physical address with identical flags, the cached length is grown by len and 0 returned; otherwise the cached extent is stored. Storing the cached extent: if entries[] is already full (entries_pos == entries_size) it sets cache->next_search_offset to the end of the last array entry, sets cache->cached = false and returns BTRFS_FIEMAP_FLUSH_CACHE without recording the cached or new extent (the caller must flush and re-search); otherwise the cached extent is appended to cache->entries (entries_pos and extents_mapped incremented) and, if extents_mapped now equals fieinfo->fi_extents_max, cache->cached = false and 1 is returned without caching the new extent; otherwise the (possibly trimmed) new extent becomes the cached one (cache->cached = true) and 0 is returned. No lock is taken.
note: fiemap.c:152-176 offset==cache->offset -> goto assign (replace); offset>cache->offset -> cache->len = offset - cache->offset; goto emit (cut cached length); offset<cache->offset -> ignore/trim new (176-196). Prose tightened with the cache_end > offset condition.

name: afs_fileserver_probe_result
prose: Precondition: call is a completed FS.GetCapabilities probe call with call->probe a live endpoint state whose address list has an entry at call->probe_index, call->server the probed server, call->net valid, and estate->nr_probing >= 1; the caller holds no server->probe_lock. Postcondition: returns nothing. It stores call->error in the addressed address's last_error, then under server->probe_lock classifies the result. error 0: estate->error = 0 and the address is marked as responded. error -ECONNABORTED: marked as responded too and, unless the estate already has AFS_ESTATE_RESPONDED, estate->abort_code = call->abort_code and estate->error = -ECONNABORTED. 'Marked as responded' means: the failed_set bit is cleared; if call->service_id == YFS_FS_SERVICE then AFS_ESTATE_IS_YFS and server AFS_SERVER_FL_IS_YFS are set and server->service_id = call->service_id; otherwise AFS_ESTATE_NOT_YFS is set, if the estate is not IS_YFS the server IS_YFS flag is cleared and server->service_id = call->service_id, and (whether or not the estate is IS_YFS) the server HAS_FS64 flag is set or cleared according to the 64-bit-files capability bit of the capability word call->tmp; then the smoothed rtt of the address peer (rxrpc_kernel_get_srtt) is read and, only when it is smaller than estate->rtt, estate->rtt and server->rtt are set to it and alist->preferred is set to the address INDEX (call->probe_index, not the rtt); finally AFS_ESTATE_RESPONDED, the responsive_set bit for the index and the server AFS_SERVER_FL_RESPONDING are set. error -ENOMEM or -ENONET: the responsive_set bit is cleared and AFS_ESTATE_LOCAL_FAILURE is set; failed_set and estate->error are not changed. Any other error (including -ECONNRESET, -ERFKILL, -EADDRNOTAVAIL, -ENETUNREACH, -EHOSTUNREACH, -EHOSTDOWN, -ECONNREFUSED, -ETIMEDOUT, -ETIME): the responsive bit is cleared, the failed_set bit is set, and estate->error = call->error only if the estate has not responded and estate->error is 0, -ETIMEDOUT or -ETIME. In every case the lock is released, the probe is traced and then afs_done_one_fs_probe runs: estate->nr_probing is decremented and, when it reaches 0, the probe set is finished under the net->fs_lock write seqlock (if the estate responded the server goes on the slow probe list, else server->rtt = UINT_MAX, AFS_SERVER_FL_RESPONDING is cleared and the server goes on the fast list) and a follow-up probe timer is scheduled (only if net->live); server->probe_wq is woken on every call, whether or not nr_probing reached 0. No reference is taken or released.
note: fs_probe.c:222-227 alist->preferred = index (not srtt); HAS_FS64 updated in the else branch regardless of estate IS_YFS (196-206)

name: btrfs_prealloc_file_range
prose: Precondition: inode is a btrfs inode, mode is a fallocate mode mask, [start, start + num_bytes) is the range to preallocate with its data space already reserved, min_size is the minimum extent size, actual_len is the requested file length and alloc_hint points to a writable u64. Postcondition: this wrapper calls __btrfs_prealloc_file_range with no transaction handle, so each iteration starts (inside btrfs_replace_file_extents) and ends its own transaction. While num_bytes > 0 each iteration requests min(num_bytes, 256MiB), raised to at least min_size, then limited to the size of the previous allocation, and reserves an extent with btrfs_reserve_extent at *alloc_hint; it inserts a PREALLOC file extent item for it (insert_prealloc_file_extent), adds a prealloc extent map (if allocating the extent map fails the extent map range is dropped and the inode is flagged for a full sync, without failing; an error from btrfs_replace_extent_map_range is overwritten by the later btrfs_update_inode result), sets *alloc_hint to the end of the extent, bumps iversion and ctime, sets BTRFS_INODE_PREALLOC, and, only if FALLOC_FL_KEEP_SIZE is not set, actual_len > i_size and the new cur_offset > i_size, sets i_size (and the safe disk i_size) to min(cur_offset, actual_len); it then calls btrfs_update_inode and, since the transaction is the function's own, ends it. The result is 0 when the whole range has been preallocated (or num_bytes is 0), else a negative errno: from btrfs_reserve_extent (for example -ENOSPC), from insert_prealloc_file_extent (the extent just reserved is freed with btrfs_free_reserved_extent), or from btrfs_update_inode (the function then aborts the transaction and ends it). On failure only a prefix of the range has been preallocated. After the loop, in every case, if clear_offset (start plus the sizes of all extents reserved, including one whose item insertion failed) is below the end of the range, the reserved data space of the rest is released with btrfs_free_reserved_data_space. No transaction remains open after return.
note: inode.c:9245-9255 condition is actual_len > i_size && cur_offset > i_size, i_size = min(cur_offset, actual_len)

name: radix_sort
prose: Precondition: array and array_buf each point to at least num valid struct bucket_item entries (array_buf is scratch of the same size), num >= 1 (array[0].count is read unconditionally) and the maximum count in array is nonzero (ilog2 of 0 is undefined). Postcondition: returns nothing. Let bitlen = ALIGN(ilog2(max count), 8), where max count is the largest array[i].count. If bitlen == 0 (which happens exactly when the maximum count is 1) no pass runs: array and array_buf are left completely unchanged. Otherwise array_buf is overwritten with intermediate results (contents unspecified on return) and the entries of array are rearranged (a permutation of the same items, no entry lost or duplicated) by a stable LSD radix sort using 4-bit digits (two passes per loop iteration, so the last pass writes back into array) over the low bitlen bits of count, with each digit inverted so that larger digits come first. Entries are therefore ordered by count mod 2^bitlen in non-increasing order; the bits at position bitlen and above are not examined, so the result is fully sorted by count only if every count is below 2^bitlen; for example a maximum count of 1 leaves array unchanged and a maximum in the range 256-511 leaves bit 8 unsorted. No lock, reference or allocation is involved.
note: compression.c:1337-1345 bitlen = ALIGN(ilog2(max_num), 8); while (shift < bitlen) is the only place array_buf is written, so with max count 1 (bitlen 0) nothing is written; reviewer right on array_buf, old prose already said array unchanged

name: btrfs_truncate_inode_items
prose: Precondition: trans is a valid write transaction handle, root is the subvolume root, control points to a struct btrfs_truncate_control whose ino, new_size and min_type are set (min_type is BTRFS_EXTENT_DATA_KEY whenever new_size != 0), and control->inode is non-NULL if control->clear_extent_range is set. Postcondition: control->last_size is first set to new_size and control->sub_bytes to 0. The function allocates a path (returns -ENOMEM if that fails) and walks the items of inode control->ino backwards from the highest key, using btrfs_search_slot, until it meets an item of another objectid, an item whose type is below min_type, or an EXTENT_DATA item whose last byte is below new_size. Items of a type above min_type, and EXTENT_DATA items starting at or after new_size, are deleted (batched through btrfs_del_items; for each deleted item control->last_size becomes its key offset); a regular or prealloc extent that straddles new_size is shrunk in place to a sector-aligned length and the walk stops with last_size = new_size; an unencoded uncompressed inline extent that straddles new_size is truncated in place, while an encoded or compressed inline extent that would need truncating makes the walk stop with the positive return value BTRFS_NEED_TRUNCATE_BLOCK. control->extents_found is incremented per EXTENT_DATA item visited, control->sub_bytes accumulates the bytes removed, the file extent range is cleared via btrfs_inode_clear_file_extent_range when control->clear_extent_range is set, and for each deleted extent with a non-zero disk bytenr (unless control->skip_ref_updates) a data ref is dropped with btrfs_free_extent. Any pending batched deletion is flushed before returning when the result so far is >= 0, and if the final result is 0 and last_size > new_size it is clamped to new_size. Returns 0 on success, BTRFS_NEED_TRUNCATE_BLOCK (positive) in the encoded-inline case, -EAGAIN when, on a shareable root, more than 32MiB of extents were freed and the transaction should end or the delayed refs reservation could not be refilled without flushing, or a negative errno from btrfs_search_slot, btrfs_inode_clear_file_extent_range, btrfs_free_extent or btrfs_del_items (the last three also abort the transaction). The path allocated at the start is freed on every return after its allocation (it is declared with BTRFS_PATH_AUTO_FREE, a scope-exit cleanup).
note: inode-item.c:~452 BTRFS_PATH_AUTO_FREE(path) (ctree.h:85, DEFINE_FREE btrfs_free_path) frees the path automatically at every return after allocation, incl. via out:. Wording tightened (deleted item, auto-free).

name: load_flat_file
prose: Real function load_flat_file(bprm, libinfo, extra_stack) in fs/binfmt_flat.c (slice starts in the middle, so the name is not in the slice). Precondition: bprm->buf holds the flat header, bprm->file is open, libinfo is valid, extra_stack is NULL or points to the extra stack size (which is increased by the header's stack_size and written back before any check). Postcondition: returns 0 with text and data mapped (or copied to RAM, decompressed if flagged), mm->start_code/end_code/start_data/end_data/start_brk/brk set, libinfo->lib_list[0] filled in, all relocations applied, the icache flushed, and the bss, brk and stack areas zeroed. Failures return a negative errno: -ENOEXEC (bad magic, bad version, any header length or count field >= 2^28, ZFLAT flags without ZFLAT support, or a relocation address that calc_reloc rejects); -ENOMEM (data+bss over RLIMIT_DATA, a vm_mmap that returns 0, or a failed vmalloc of the decompression buffer); the error returned by begin_new_exec (called just before the slice; setup_new_exec after it returns void), vm_mmap, read_code, decompress_exec, flat_get_addr_from_rp or flat_put_addr_at_rp (the generic versions return 0 or -EFAULT); or -EFAULT from a failing get_user, put_user, copy_to_user or clear_user. The data-load failures unmap the mappings made so far (vm_munmap), but relocation errors and -EFAULT returns do not unmap them. A vmalloc'd decompression buffer is freed on every path. Once begin_new_exec has succeeded (the point of no return) the old image is gone, so any later failure leaves the caller to kill the process.
note: Reviewer claim wrong: begin_new_exec(bprm) is called at binfmt_flat.c:~504 inside the function (just before the slice); setup_new_exec (void) is separate. Real error fixed: flat_get_addr_from_rp/flat_put_addr_at_rp return 0 or -EFAULT (include/asm-generic/flat.h:11-22), not -ENOEXEC.

name: venus_access_intent
prose: Precondition: sb is a valid coda superblock, fid points to a valid CodaFid, access_intent_supported points to a bool that records whether Venus supports chunked access, count, ppos and type describe the access, and type is a CODA_ACCESS_TYPE_* value. Postcondition: if *access_intent_supported is false and type is neither CODA_ACCESS_TYPE_READ_FINISH nor CODA_ACCESS_TYPE_WRITE_FINISH it returns 0 without sending anything. Otherwise it allocates the message, returning -ENOMEM if that fails, and sends a CODA_ACCESS_INTENT upcall: for the two FINISH types the upcall is asynchronous (outsize NULL), and the message buffer is NOT freed here when the upcall succeeds (ownership passes to the queued request) but IS freed when it fails; for other types the upcall is synchronous and the buffer is always freed. If the upcall's result is -EOPNOTSUPP, *access_intent_supported is set to false and 0 is returned; otherwise the result of the upcall is returned (0 on success, -ENXIO if Venus is not running, -ENOMEM, -EINTR, or the negated Venus error for synchronous upcalls).
note: Checked against upcall.c venus_access_intent: UPARG returns PTR_ERR on alloc failure; kvfree only if !finalizer||error; EOPNOTSUPP->0.

name: errno_to_blk_status
prose: Precondition: none; errno may be any int. Postcondition: the function returns the blk_status_t whose value is the index of the first entry of the designated-initialiser table blk_errors whose errno field equals the argument, and BLK_STS_IOERR (10) when no entry matches. The mapping is: 0 -> 0 (BLK_STS_OK), -EOPNOTSUPP -> 1, -ETIMEDOUT -> 2, -ENOSPC -> 3, -ENOLINK -> 4, -EREMOTEIO -> 5, -EBADE -> 6, -ENODATA -> 7, -EILSEQ -> 8, -ENOMEM -> 9, -EIO -> 10, -EREMCHG -> 11, -EAGAIN -> 12, -EBUSY -> 13, -ETOOMANYREFS -> 14, -EOVERFLOW -> 15, -ENODEV -> 16, -ETIME -> 17, -EINVAL -> 19 (index 18 of the table is unused and holds errno 0, so it is never selected because index 0 matches first), and every other value -> 10. It has no side effects and acquires or releases no lock, reference or memory.
contract: /*@ requires \true; ensures (errno == 0 ? result == 0 : errno == -95 ? result == 1 : errno == -110 ? result == 2 : errno == -28 ? result == 3 : errno == -67 ? result == 4 : errno == -121 ? result == 5 : errno == -52 ? result == 6 : errno == -61 ? result == 7 : errno == -84 ? result == 8 : errno == -12 ? result == 9 : errno == -5 ? result == 10 : errno == -78 ? result == 11 : errno == -11 ? result == 12 : errno == -16 ? result == 13 : errno == -109 ? result == 14 : errno == -75 ? result == 15 : errno == -19 ? result == 16 : errno == -62 ? result == 17 : errno == -22 ? result == 19 : result == 10) && (result != 0 || errno == 0); */
note: blk-core.c blk_errors table indexed by BLK_STS_* (blk_types.h:99-171): BLK_STS_IOERR=10 (-EIO), DEV_RESOURCE=13 (-EBUSY), INVAL=19; errno numbers in the contract are the generic asm-generic values (arch-specific on alpha/mips/sparc/parisc).

name: blk_add_timer
prose: Precondition: req points to a request about to start, req->q is a valid request queue; the caller may be in any context (the timer is modified with mod_timer). Postcondition: returns nothing. If req->timeout was 0 it is set to q->rq_timeout. RQF_TIMED_OUT is cleared in req->rq_flags. Let j1 be the jiffies value read once for the deadline: req->deadline is set (WRITE_ONCE) to j1 + req->timeout (unrounded). Let expiry = blk_rq_timeout(blk_round_jiffies(j1 + req->timeout)), where blk_round_jiffies(x) = x + roundup_pow_of_two(HZ) and blk_rq_timeout caps its argument at blk_round_jiffies(j2 + BLK_MAX_TIMEOUT) with j2 a SECOND, separate read of jiffies made inside blk_rq_timeout (so the cap is not computed from the same sample as j1). The queue timer q->timeout is re-armed with mod_timer(&q->timeout, expiry) if and only if either the timer is not pending, or expiry is before q->timeout.expires and q->timeout.expires - expiry >= HZ / 2. In every other case (timer pending and expiry not earlier, or earlier by less than HZ/2) the timer is left unchanged. No lock, reference or memory is acquired or released.
note: Reviewer right: blk-timeout.c blk_rq_timeout() reads jiffies again (maxt = blk_round_jiffies(jiffies + BLK_MAX_TIMEOUT)); also blk_round_jiffies adds mask+1, it is not a round to a boundary.

name: afs_wait_for_vl_probes
prose: Real function int afs_wait_for_vl_probes(vllist, untried) in fs/afs/vl_probe.c (slice starts mid-function). Precondition: vllist is a valid VL server list with nr_servers <= BITS_PER_LONG, whose servers have probes started; untried is a bitmask of server indices to consider; the caller holds no lock. Postcondition: indices of servers whose AFS_VLSERVER_FL_PROBING is clear are dropped from the local mask; if any considered server already has AFS_VLSERVER_PROBE_RESPONDED, or no considered server remains, it returns 0 immediately without changing vllist->preferred. Otherwise it returns -ENOMEM if the wait-queue array cannot be allocated (nothing changed). Else it adds a wait entry on each considered server's probe_wq and sleeps interruptibly until any considered server has responded, or none is still probing, or a signal is pending; it then removes all wait entries, frees the array and, among the considered servers with AFS_VLSERVER_FL_RESPONDING, picks the one with the smallest rtt. If none responded and a signal is pending it returns -ERESTARTSYS; otherwise it sets vllist->preferred to the chosen index (when one exists, else leaves it unchanged) and returns 0.
note: afs/vl_probe.c afs_wait_for_vl_probes: first loop sets have_responders from server->probe.flags & AFS_VLSERVER_PROBE_RESPONDED and 'if (have_responders || !untried) return 0;' before kmalloc; reviewer saw only the slice (the wait loop's goto stop path, which does set preferred).

name: btrfs_replace_file_extents
prose: Precondition: the caller holds the inode lock and has locked the file range [start, end]; path is a usable (empty) path in the inode's root; extent_info is NULL or describes the replacement extent; trans_out is a valid output pointer. Postcondition: returns -EINVAL, changing nothing and without touching any reservation, if end <= start. Otherwise it initialises a temporary block reservation, starts a transaction and drops every file extent overlapping [start, end], possibly over several transactions: the drop loop repeats only when btrfs_drop_extents returns -ENOSPC, in which case it commits progress (when extent_info is NULL the dropped part is replaced by hole items for the part below the rounded-up i_size, or merely cleared from the extent range map for the part at or past it; when extent_info is given and the drop end is beyond extent_info->file_offset the replacement extent is inserted piecewise), updates the inode (i_version and, when extent_info is NULL or extent_info->update_times, mtime/ctime) and ends the transaction before starting a new one. After the loop it fills the remainder with holes (extent_info NULL, below rounded i_size) or clears the range (extent_info NULL, past i_size), or inserts the rest of the replacement extent (extent_info non-NULL). If extent_info is non-NULL and not a new extent, the inode is marked for a full fsync, even when the function goes on to fail. Returns 0 on success, with *trans_out set to the live transaction, which the caller must end. On failure it returns a negative errno (from starting a transaction, migrating the block reservation, dropping extents, filling holes, clearing the range, inserting the replacement extent, updating the inode, or finding the next non-hole), aborts the transaction for drop errors other than -ENOSPC (except -EOPNOTSUPP when no new extent is being inserted), and for fill_holes, clear-range, insert-replace and inode-update errors; start-transaction, reservation-migrate and find_first_non_hole errors do not abort. On failure any live transaction is ended by the function and *trans_out is left unset. Once the reservation has been initialised, it is released before every return.
note: Verified against file.c btrfs_replace_file_extents: abort condition is ret != -ENOSPC && ret && (ret != -EOPNOTSUPP || (extent_info && is_new_extent)); full_sync set before 'if (ret) goto out_trans'; -EINVAL return precedes btrfs_init_metadata_block_rsv. Prose tightened accordingly.

name: btrfs_device_set_##name
prose: Generated by BTRFS_DEVICE_GETSET_FUNCS(name) as btrfs_device_set_<name>(dev, size) for a u64 field of struct btrfs_device. Precondition: dev is a valid btrfs_device and the caller serialises concurrent writers of the field (no lock is taken here). Postcondition: dev->name equals size; returns nothing; the only other state touched is the sequence counter dev->data_seqcount (incremented twice, by write_seqcount_begin and write_seqcount_end) on a 32-bit SMP build, and the preempt count, which is raised and lowered again. No other field of dev changes. On a 32-bit SMP build the store is done with preemption disabled inside a write_seqcount_begin/end pair on dev->data_seqcount so readers retry instead of seeing a torn value; on a 32-bit preemptible (CONFIG_PREEMPTION, non-SMP) build the store is done with preemption disabled; on other builds it is a plain store and data_seqcount does not exist. Preemption is re-enabled before returning.
note: volumes.h BTRFS_DEVICE_GETSET_FUNCS: 32-bit SMP variant does preempt_disable; write_seqcount_begin(&dev->data_seqcount); dev->name = size; write_seqcount_end; preempt_enable. Reviewer right: 'nothing else changes' ignored data_seqcount.

name: __send_flush_snap
prose: Precondition: inode, session and capsnap are valid; capsnap is kept alive by the caller (which holds a reference) and the caller does not hold ci->i_ceph_lock (the caller drops it around the call); the function takes no lock itself. Postcondition: builds a cap_msg_args from capsnap (op CEPH_CAP_OP_FLUSHSNAP, follows, flush tid, sizes, times, mode, uid/gid, inline data, oldest_flush_tid and mseq as passed); allocates a message with ceph_msg_new(CEPH_MSG_CLIENT_CAPS, ..., GFP_NOFS): if the allocation fails returns -ENOMEM and sends nothing; otherwise encodes the message, hands it to ceph_con_send on session->s_con (which takes the connection's own locking internally) and returns 0. It takes or releases no reference and does not modify capsnap or the inode.
note: caps.c __send_flush_snap lines 42-99 of the slice: ceph_msg_new failure -> -ENOMEM; else encode_cap_msg + ceph_con_send; caller __ceph_flush_snaps drops i_ceph_lock at spin_unlock before the call. Reworded 'no locks' since ceph_con_send locks internally.

name: __ceph_flush_snaps
prose: Precondition: the caller holds ci->i_ceph_lock and session is a valid session reference held by the caller. Postcondition: returns void with ci->i_ceph_lock held again (it is dropped around each message send and re-taken). First pass: walks ci->i_cap_snaps from the head. For each capsnap: if it has dirty_pages or writing set the walk stops (this and later capsnaps are not flushed); otherwise it does BUG_ON(!capsnap->need_flush) (so this applies to every capsnap reached, including ones skipped next); a capsnap whose cap_flush.tid is already non-zero is skipped; any other capsnap gets a new tid ++mdsc->last_cap_flush_tid and is appended to mdsc->cap_flush_list (and oldest_flush_tid is set once from __get_oldest_flush_tid) and ci is appended to session->s_cap_flushing if ci->i_flushing_item is empty, all under mdsc->cap_dirty_lock; after that lock is released the capsnap is appended to ci->i_cap_flush_list and the first/last tid range is updated. It then clears CEPH_I_FLUSH_SNAPS on ci (always, even if no capsnap was queued or later sends fail). Second pass: while first_tid <= last_tid: if ci->i_auth_cap is NULL or its session is not session it stops; it looks up the first entry of ci->i_cap_flush_list with tid >= first_tid (it stops if there is none; this lookup is not bounded above by last_tid), sets first_tid to that tid + 1, takes a reference on the containing capsnap (refcount_inc nref), drops i_ceph_lock, sends it with __send_flush_snap using the auth cap's mseq and oldest_flush_tid (an error, i.e. -ENOMEM, is only logged with pr_err_client and not retried), puts the capsnap reference with ceph_put_cap_snap and retakes the lock. Not every queued capsnap is necessarily sent (a send may fail, or the loop may stop because the auth cap changed or is missing).
note: caps.c __ceph_flush_snaps: BUG_ON(!need_flush) precedes the tid>0 skip; i_cap_flush_list add is after cap_dirty_lock is released; the second-pass lookup is 'iter->tid >= first_tid' with no upper bound. Prose corrected on those points.

name: BTRFS_SETGET_FUNCS(inode_size, struct btrfs_inode_item, size, 64)
prose: Generated pair of inline accessors for the 64-bit size field of struct btrfs_inode_item: btrfs_inode_size(eb, s) and btrfs_set_inode_size(eb, s, val); the name field is the macro invocation that generates them. Precondition: eb is a valid extent buffer; s is the offset of an inode item within eb (an offset cast to a pointer, not a real address). Postcondition: btrfs_inode_size returns btrfs_get_64(eb, s, offsetof(struct btrfs_inode_item, size)): the little-endian 64-bit size stored in the item, or 0 after a bounds warning if the field lies outside eb->len. btrfs_set_inode_size stores val little-endian in that field through btrfs_set_64, and writes nothing (with a bounds warning) if the field lies outside eb->len. Neither takes a lock or reference; the getter does not modify the buffer.
note: accessors.h:62-74 macro and accessors.c DEFINE_BTRFS_SETGET_BITS: bounds check returns 0 / writes nothing after report_setget_bounds.

name: cache_save_setup
prose: Precondition: block_group, trans and path are valid; path is an empty caller-owned path; the caller holds no block_group->lock. Postcondition: returns 0 without touching block_group->disk_cache_state or cache_generation if the SPACE_CACHE mount option is off; returns 0 after setting disk_cache_state = BTRFS_DC_WRITTEN if block_group->length < 100 MiB; returns 0 without touching the state if the transaction is already aborted (this test comes after the length test). On all other paths it computes a state dcs (initially BTRFS_DC_ERROR) and, at the end, always (not conditionally) stores block_group->disk_cache_state = dcs under block_group->lock, and also sets cache_generation = trans->transid when the result is 0 and dcs == BTRFS_DC_SETUP; it also frees the data reservation changeset and releases the path, and drops the inode reference if one was held. Outcomes: the lookup of the free space inode fails with an error other than -ENOENT: returns that error (dcs ERROR); the inode is missing and the block group is read-only: returns 0 with dcs ERROR; otherwise the inode is created (error returned, dcs ERROR) and looked up again (a second miss is a BUG()); updating the inode with generation 0 fails: the transaction is aborted and that error returned (dcs ERROR); the inode already has size and cache_generation == trans->transid: returns 0 with dcs SETUP; truncating a non-empty cache (btrfs_check_trunc_cache_free_space / btrfs_truncate_free_space_cache) fails: its error is returned (dcs ERROR); the group is not BTRFS_CACHE_FINISHED or SPACE_CACHE is off: returns 0 with dcs WRITTEN; BTRFS_TRANS_CACHE_ENOSPC already set on the transaction: returns -ENOSPC (dcs ERROR); btrfs_check_data_free_space failure: its error returned; preallocation success: returns 0 with dcs SETUP; preallocation failure: returns its error, and -ENOSPC additionally sets BTRFS_TRANS_CACHE_ENOSPC in trans->transaction->flags. May create or truncate the free space inode; the caller keeps ownership of trans and path.
note: block-group.c:3346-3352 label out: unconditionally 'block_group->disk_cache_state = dcs' under block_group->lock for every path reaching out; only cache_generation is conditional (!ret && dcs == BTRFS_DC_SETUP). Early returns (SPACE_CACHE off, <100MiB, aborted) are before out and described separately.

name: btrfs_bg_flags_to_raid_index
prose: Precondition: none, flags is any u64 block group flags value. Postcondition: let profile = flags & BTRFS_BLOCK_GROUP_PROFILE_MASK (bits 3 to 10: RAID0, RAID1, DUP, RAID10, RAID5, RAID6, RAID1C3, RAID1C4). If profile is 0 the result is BTRFS_RAID_SINGLE (0). Otherwise the result is ilog2(profile >> 2), that is the position of the highest set profile bit minus 2: RAID0 gives 1, RAID1 2, DUP 3, RAID10 4, RAID5 5, RAID6 6, RAID1C3 7 and RAID1C4 8 when exactly one profile bit is set, and when several profile bits are set the highest bit decides. The result is always in [0, 8], below BTRFS_NR_RAID_TYPES (9). It is a pure function with no lock, reference or memory effect.
note: volumes.h:59-61 enum: BTRFS_RAID_SINGLE = 0 explicitly; BTRFS_BG_FLAG_TO_INDEX(p) = ilog2(p >> (ilog2(RAID0)-1)) = ilog2(p >> 2) with RAID0 = 1<<3 (btrfs_tree.h:1156-1163); PROFILE_MASK = 0x7f8 = 2040.

name: EXT4_FEATURE_COMPAT_FUNCS(journal,		HAS_JOURNAL)
prose: Generated function ext4_has_feature_journal(sb) (one of the three inline functions that the macro invocation EXT4_FEATURE_COMPAT_FUNCS(journal, HAS_JOURNAL) defines). Precondition: sb is a valid ext4 super_block whose EXT4_SB(sb)->s_es on-disk superblock copy is valid and readable. Postcondition: returns true if and only if the EXT4_FEATURE_COMPAT_HAS_JOURNAL bit (0x0004) is set in s_es->s_feature_compat (compared after cpu_to_le32 conversion), otherwise false; it modifies no state and takes no lock.
note: ext4.h:2141-2146 EXT4_FEATURE_COMPAT_FUNCS: returns (s_es->s_feature_compat & cpu_to_le32(EXT4_FEATURE_COMPAT_HAS_JOURNAL)) != 0.

name: ext4_set_context
prose: Precondition: inode is an ext4 inode, ctx points to a valid fscrypt encryption context of len bytes, and fs_data is either NULL (set the context on an existing inode, in its own transaction) or a journal handle_t for a larger transaction creating a new inode (the inode already has the encrypt flag set and must not have EXT4_STATE_MAY_INLINE_DATA). Postcondition: returns 0 or a negative errno. It first fails with -EPERM if inode is the root inode (inode number EXT4_ROOT_INO), -EINVAL (with WARN_ON_ONCE) if S_DAX is set, or -EOPNOTSUPP if the EXT4_INODE_DAX flag is set; none of these changes anything. It then calls ext4_convert_inline_data and returns its error if non-zero (a successful conversion of inline data stays done even if a later step fails). If fs_data (handle) is non-NULL it additionally returns -EINVAL (with WARN_ON_ONCE) if the inode is not IS_ENCRYPTED or has EXT4_STATE_MAY_INLINE_DATA set; otherwise it returns just the result of ext4_xattr_set_handle(handle, inode, EXT4_XATTR_INDEX_ENCRYPTION, ..., ctx, len, XATTR_CREATE), without touching the ENCRYPT inode flag, S_ENCRYPTED or the inode's dirty state (the caller handles those) and without stopping the caller's handle. If fs_data is NULL it calls dquot_initialize (its error returned), computes the xattr journal credits with ext4_xattr_set_credits (error returned), starts its own journal handle with ext4_journal_start (PTR_ERR of failure returned) and calls ext4_xattr_set_handle with flag 0; if that returns 0 it sets EXT4_INODE_ENCRYPT, updates inode->i_flags (S_ENCRYPTED) and calls ext4_mark_inode_dirty (a failure there is logged with EXT4_ERROR_INODE and becomes the result). It then always stops its handle with ext4_journal_stop (result res2). If the result so far is -ENOSPC (from either the xattr set or ext4_mark_inode_dirty) and ext4_should_retry_alloc allows it, the whole sequence from the credit computation is retried; otherwise the result is that error, or, if it is 0, the result of ext4_journal_stop. So with fs_data NULL a negative return can happen after the ENCRYPT flag was set (mark-dirty or journal-stop failure).
note: crypto.c ext4_set_context: 'if (res == -ENOSPC && ext4_should_retry_alloc(...)) goto retry;' tests res after both xattr set and mark_inode_dirty. Reviewer right. Also fixed 'changing nothing' claim vs ext4_convert_inline_data, and added dquot/credit/stop details.

name: COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE6(io_pgetevents_time64,
