name: v9fs_vfs_atomic_open_dotl
prose: Real function v9fs_vfs_atomic_open_dotl(dir, dentry, file, flags, omode) in fs/9p/vfs_inode_dotl.c (the slice starts in its middle, after the lookup and O_CREAT checks; the function that is literally named v9fs_vfs_create_dotl is a different, 3-line wrapper that just returns v9fs_vfs_mknod_dotl(idmap, dir, dentry, omode, 0) and is not what the slice contains). Precondition: dir is a directory inode on a 9p mount, dentry is a dentry of the entry to open in it, file is the struct file being opened; the function may sleep. Postcondition, returns an int: if the dentry is in lookup state and v9fs_vfs_lookup returns a non-NULL result or leaves the dentry positive, it returns finish_no_open(file, res); otherwise, if O_CREAT is not set in flags, it returns finish_no_open(file, NULL); in neither case is anything created. Otherwise it creates and opens the file: gets the parent fid (v9fs_parent_fid), clones it (clone_fid) as the open fid ofid, computes the creation gid and the mode adjusted by the directory's default ACL (v9fs_acl_mode), converts the open flags to 9P flags (a write-only open is turned into read-write without append when the mount has CACHE_WRITEBACK), and sends Tlcreate (p9_client_create_dotl), then invalidates the directory's cached attributes, walks the parent fid to the new name to get an unopened fid, obtains a new inode from that fid (v9fs_get_new_inode_from_fid), sets the ACLs on it from the default ACL values, attaches the unopened fid to the dentry (v9fs_fid_add) and instantiates the dentry with the inode (d_instantiate), then calls finish_open(file, dentry, generic_file_open). On success (err 0) file->private_data is set to ofid, the fscache cookie is used (when CACHE_FSCACHE and CONFIG_9P_FSCACHE), the open fid gets its cache/mode flags and is added to the inode's open fid list (v9fs_open_fid_add), FMODE_CREATED is set in file->f_mode, and it returns 0. On failure it returns the negative errno of the first failing step (parent fid lookup, fid clone, ACL mode computation, p9_client_create_dotl, the walk, inode creation, or finish_open); it fails before instantiating the dentry in all cases except finish_open, after which the dentry is already instantiated with the new inode, and if the server-side create already succeeded the file still exists on the server. On every path after the create-checks, the parent fid, the open fid and the new fid are dropped with p9_fid_put unless they were handed over to the dentry or inode (which sets those pointers to NULL), and the ACL references are released with v9fs_put_acl.
note: vfs_inode_dotl.c: slice is the tail of v9fs_vfs_atomic_open_dotl (starts line 226); v9fs_vfs_create_dotl is at line 220-224 (return v9fs_vfs_mknod_dotl(..., 0)). Reviewer right: first-pass prose described the wrong function.

name: ext4_ext_insert_extent
prose: Real function ext4_ext_insert_extent(handle, inode, path, newext, gb_flags) (the slice begins in the middle of it; the packet suffix '(tail; name elided in excerpt)' is not part of the name). Precondition: handle is an active journal handle with enough credits, path is the path returned by ext4_find_extent for the logical block of newext (valid down to the leaf at ext_depth(inode)) and is owned by the caller, newext points to a valid extent to insert whose block range does not overlap an existing extent, and gb_flags holds EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_* flags. Postcondition: returns a struct ext4_ext_path * or an ERR_PTR. On success the returned path (which may be a different path from the one passed in: the old one is then freed, e.g. when the next leaf or a newly created leaf is used) is owned by the caller, and newext has been merged with an adjacent extent (unless gb_flags has EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_PRE_IO, which skips merging) or inserted in sorted position in the leaf, eh_entries incremented, the indexes above corrected and the leaf buffer marked dirty (ext4_ext_dirty). On failure it returns ERR_PTR(err) and the caller must not use or free the path it passed in: -EFSCORRUPTED if newext has actual length 0 or path[depth].p_hdr is NULL (after EXT4_ERROR_INODE), or the error of ext4_ext_get_access, ext4_find_extent (looking for the next leaf), ext4_ext_create_new_leaf (e.g. -ENOSPC; it returns the error path itself), ext4_ext_correct_indexes or ext4_ext_dirty; except that for the create-new-leaf failure the path is as released by that function. The in-memory extent leaf may already have been modified when a late step (index correction or dirtying) fails.
note: extents.c ext4_ext_insert_extent: 'if (ex && !(gb_flags & EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_PRE_IO)) { ...append / prepend merge... }' skips the append/prepend merge under PRE_IO, and 'merge:' does 'if (!(gb_flags & PRE_IO)) ext4_ext_try_to_merge()'; so PRE_IO skips all merging.

name: de_thread
prose: Precondition: tsk is the current task, about to complete an exec, and tsk->signal and tsk->sighand are valid; the caller holds no siglock or tasklist_lock and may sleep. Postcondition: returns 0 or -EAGAIN. If the thread group has only tsk (thread_group_empty) it just sets tsk->exit_signal = SIGCHLD and returns 0. Otherwise, under the sighand siglock: if the group is already exiting (SIGNAL_GROUP_EXIT) or another task is already exec-ing (sig->group_exec_task non-NULL) it returns -EAGAIN with no state changed; else it sets sig->group_exec_task = tsk, kills all other threads (zap_other_threads) and sleeps killably until they have exited (notify_count reaches 0). If a fatal signal becomes pending during either wait (waiting for the other threads, or for the old leader to become a zombie) it takes tasklist_lock for reading, resets sig->group_exec_task = NULL and sig->notify_count = 0, and returns -EAGAIN (the state it set is unwound; other threads may already have been killed). If tsk was not the group leader it waits for the old leader to exit, then under tasklist_lock (write) and the cgroup threadgroup lock it takes over the leader's start_time/start_boottime, swaps tids with it (exchange_tids), transfers its TGID, PGID and SID pids, replaces it in the tasks/sibling lists, becomes the group leader with exit_signal SIGCHLD, marks the old leader EXIT_DEAD and releases it with release_task(). On success it resets sig->group_exec_task = NULL and sig->notify_count = 0, sets tsk->exit_signal = SIGCHLD, and returns 0 with tsk the sole thread and group leader and no lock held.
note: exec.c de_thread: label killed: read_lock(&tasklist_lock) (not write); the write_lock_irq(&tasklist_lock) is only in the leader-wait/identity-swap loop; label no_thread_group: 'tsk->exit_signal = SIGCHLD;' before BUG_ON(!thread_group_leader) and return 0.

name: coda_upcall
prose: Real function is coda_upcall(vcp, inSize, outSize, buffer) (the slice only contains its prototype, the body is later in upcall.c). Precondition: the caller does not hold vcp->vc_mutex; buffer is a complete input message of inSize bytes allocated by the caller (alloc_upcall) with a valid inputArgs header; outSize is NULL for an asynchronous request or points to an int holding the expected reply size (0 meaning inSize) for a synchronous one. Postcondition: takes vcp->vc_mutex and releases it before returning. If vcp->vc_inuse is 0 it returns -ENXIO and if the request structure cannot be allocated it returns -ENOMEM, in both cases with nothing queued and buffer still owned by the caller. Otherwise it stamps buffer->ih.unique with ++vcp->vc_seq, queues the request on vcp->vc_pending and wakes Venus. If outSize is NULL it returns 0 at once; the request now owns buffer, which the caller must not free (it is freed after Venus reads it). If outSize is non-NULL it waits (coda_waitfor_upcall): if Venus replied (CODA_REQ_WRITE) it sets *outSize to the reply size and returns -(reply result) (0 on success, the negated Venus error otherwise); if the wait ended for another reason it returns -EINTR (also when it was aborted by Venus shutdown or woke without a pending signal); when interrupted after Venus had read the request it additionally queues a CODA_SIGNAL message at the head of the pending list, but returns -ENOMEM instead of -EINTR if that signal request cannot be allocated, and queues nothing if Venus has since died. In all synchronous cases the request structure is freed here and buffer remains owned by the caller (it holds the reply when one arrived).
note: coda_upcall body at upcall.c:709-806 verified against every claim

name: TLV_PUT_DEFINE_INT(8)
prose: Generated function tlv_put_u8(sctx, attr, value), where attr has type u8 (and is widened to the u16 attribute type) and value is a u8: Precondition: sctx is a valid send context. Postcondition: it copies value into a local one-byte temporary __tmp (cpu_to_le8, an identity) and returns tlv_put(sctx, attr, &__tmp, 1). If sctx->put_data is set it returns -EINVAL (with a one-time warning); else if fewer than 4 + 1 bytes remain (send_max_size - send_size < 5) it returns -EOVERFLOW; in both failure cases sctx->send_buf and send_size are unchanged. Otherwise it appends a little-endian TLV header (type attr, length 1) followed by the single byte value at send_buf + send_size, increases send_size by 5 and returns 0. No lock, reference or allocation is involved.
note: Reviewer right: send.c:~609 tlv_put_u8 passes &__tmp (local __le8 copy of value), not &value; rest of prose checked vs tlv_put.

name: _aead_recvmsg
prose: Precondition: sock->sk is an AF_ALG AEAD socket (with its parent socket holding the aead transform) and the caller holds lock_sock on it; the function may sleep. Postcondition: if ctx->init is false or ctx->more is set it first calls af_alg_wait_for_data and returns any non-zero error from it (for example -EAGAIN) with nothing allocated. Then it returns -EINVAL, again with nothing allocated, if ctx->used < aead_assoclen + (tag size when decrypting). Otherwise outlen = used + tag size (encrypt) or used - tag size (decrypt), where used includes the AAD, and the input length used is reduced by aead_assoclen. It allocates the async request with af_alg_alloc_areq; if that fails it returns the error (nothing to free). From here on, every failure and the normal end go through one cleanup that calls af_alg_free_resources(areq), except the -EIOCBQUEUED return. It copies the IV, obtains the output scatterlist with af_alg_get_rsgl (on error: cleanup, returning that error); if the caller output space (usedpages) is smaller than outlen it computes the shortfall and returns -EINVAL (after cleanup) if used < shortfall + (tag size when decrypting), else reduces used and outlen by the shortfall. It then allocates the TX scatterlist for processed = used + aead_assoclen bytes (-ENOMEM after cleanup on failure), pulls exactly those processed bytes (AAD plus input) out of the socket TX list, copies the AAD to the output and submits encrypt or decrypt. For an asynchronous kiocb it takes an extra sock reference and sets areq->iocb and areq->outlen; if the operation returns -EINPROGRESS the function returns -EIOCBQUEUED immediately without calling af_alg_free_resources (the request resources and the sock reference are released later by af_alg_async_cb); otherwise (completed or failed at once) the extra sock reference is dropped and it goes to cleanup. For a synchronous request it waits with crypto_wait_req. After cleanup it returns the error (for example -EBADMSG for a failed authentication tag) if non-zero, else outlen (the number of bytes written to the caller output).
note: Reviewer right: algif_aead.c: returns before the free label (wait_for_data error, !aead_sufficient_data -EINVAL, IS_ERR(areq)) do not call af_alg_free_resources; -EIOCBQUEUED return skips it too.

name: afs_update_volume_creation_time
prose: Precondition: op is a valid afs_operation whose pre_volsync.creation (old) and volsync.creation (new) hold the creation times before and after the operation; volume is a valid afs_volume; the caller holds no lock this function takes. Postcondition: returns 0 and sets volume->creation_time = new, without anything else, if volume->creation_time was TIME64_MIN; returns 0 changing nothing if new equals the current creation_time or if the current creation_time (cur) differs from old (another operation already advanced it). Otherwise (cur == old and new != cur): for an RW volume, and for a Backup volume when new < old, it does atomic_inc(&volume->cb_scrub), emits the creation-regress trace, sets volume->creation_time = new and returns 0. For a Backup volume with new >= old it does atomic_inc_return(&volume->cb_ro_snapshot), emits the vos-release trace, sets volume->creation_time = new and returns 0. For any other (RO) volume it first calls afs_is_server_excluded(op, volume). That helper returns 1 at once if op->server is excluded in the volume server list; otherwise it sets AFS_VOLUME_NEEDS_UPDATE on the volume and calls afs_check_volume_status (which may sleep and refresh the volume status from the VL server, and may itself set or clear that flag), returning its negative errno if that fails, else whether the server is now excluded (0 or 1). If the helper returns a negative errno, this function returns it, leaving cb_scrub, cb_ro_snapshot and creation_time unchanged, but AFS_VOLUME_NEEDS_UPDATE may have been set and the volume status may have been updated. If it returns a positive value it emits the volume-excluded trace and returns that value, with creation_time and the counters unchanged. If it returns 0 (server not excluded) the RO volume takes the same path as the Backup new >= old case: atomic_inc_return(&volume->cb_ro_snapshot), vos-release trace, creation_time = new, return 0. No lock or reference is left held. Increments are plain atomic increments (not a cmpxchg); the guard against races is the cur == old test.
note: Reviewer right: validation.c afs_is_server_excluded does set_bit(AFS_VOLUME_NEEDS_UPDATE) (l.~204) and afs_check_volume_status may set it again / sleep; negative errno path is not side-effect free.

name: btrfs_find_allocatable_zones
prose: Precondition: device is a zoned device with a non-NULL zone_info; hole_start and num_bytes are multiples of the zone size (both ASSERTed, which is a no-op unless assertions are enabled); hole_end is not required to be aligned or to be at least hole_start. Postcondition: returns a u64 position; it takes no lock, acquires no reference and modifies nothing. Starting at pos = hole_start, while pos < hole_end it considers the region of nzones = num_bytes / zone size zones starting at the zone of pos (bytes [pos, pos + num_bytes)). If the region would extend beyond the last zone of the device (end zone index > nr_zones) the function returns hole_end immediately; that value is returned as is and is not guaranteed to be zone-aligned. If the zone at pos is sequential and the nzones zones of the region are not all marked empty, pos advances by one zone and the search continues (when the zone at pos is conventional the emptiness of the zones is not checked). Otherwise, for each of the BTRFS_SUPER_MIRROR_MAX mirrors in order, if the region overlaps that mirror superblock-log zones (BTRFS_NR_SB_LOG_ZONES zones) pos moves to the start of the first zone after that log; else if the byte range [pos, pos + num_bytes) overlaps the regular superblock copy of that mirror (BTRFS_SUPER_INFO_SIZE bytes) pos moves to the zone-aligned position after that copy; either way the search then continues with the new pos. If the region overlaps none of them the loop stops and pos is returned. The result is therefore either hole_end (device too small, possibly unaligned), or the first candidate position that satisfies the conditions, or, when the loop ran off the end of the hole, a position at or beyond hole_end that was reached by the last advance (the caller must compare the result against hole_end). Every return value other than the early hole_end is zone-aligned.
note: Reviewer right: zoned.c:~1075 returns hole_end (no alignment guaranteed) when end > nr_zones; other returns are aligned (pos starts aligned, advances by zone_size / zone start / ALIGN).

name: btrfs_nr_parity_stripes
prose: Precondition: none, type is any u64 block group type value. Postcondition: the result is the nparity field of btrfs_raid_array for the raid type selected by btrfs_bg_flags_to_raid_index(type), which looks at the highest set profile bit of type (bits 3 to 10): 1 if that highest profile bit is the RAID5 bit, 2 if it is the RAID6 bit, and 0 in every other case (no profile bit, or a highest profile bit of RAID0, RAID1, DUP, RAID10, RAID1C3 or RAID1C4). In particular RAID5 together with RAID6 gives 2, and RAID5 together with RAID1C3 gives 0. It is a pure lookup with no lock, reference or memory effect.
note: Reviewer wrong: volumes.h:65 BTRFS_BG_FLAG_TO_INDEX = ilog2(profile >> 2) = highest set bit, so RAID5|RAID6 -> index 6 -> nparity 2; PROFILE_MASK = bits 3..10 = 2040; volumes.c:~196 only !profile gives SINGLE.

name: btrfs_init_new_device
prose: Function btrfs_init_new_device(fs_info, device_path): add the block device at device_path as a new writeable device of the mounted filesystem. Precondition: fs_info is a mounted btrfs filesystem; the caller holds no lock that the function takes (s_umount, uuid_mutex, device_list_mutex, chunk_mutex); it may sleep. Early failures, in order, with no change to the filesystem: -EROFS if the superblock is read-only and fs_devices->seeding is not set; the error of bdev_file_open_by_path (open for write with fs_holder_ops); -EINVAL if btrfs_check_device_zone_type fails; -EINVAL if the device size is not larger than BTRFS_DEVICE_RANGE_RESERVED (the opened block device reference is dropped with bdev_fput on these). Then, if fs_devices->seeding is set, it takes s_umount for writing and then uuid_mutex and keeps both until just after the first transaction commit (the point where it releases them for the seeding case); it calls sync_blockdev; it returns -EEXIST if a device with the same block device is already in fs_devices->devices; it allocates a device (btrfs_alloc_device error returned), sets the device bdev, looks up devt (lookup_bdev error), gets zone info (btrfs_get_dev_zone_info error) and starts a transaction on the dev root (its error returned). Failures in these steps free what was set up (device, zone info) and call bdev_fput, and release uuid_mutex and s_umount if they were taken. It then initialises the device (writeable, sizes from the block device rounded to the sector size, blocksize set), and for a seeding filesystem calls btrfs_init_sprout (on error: abort the transaction, end it, free zone info and device, bdev_fput, unlock, return the error). Under device_list_mutex and chunk_mutex it sprouts the seed devices (seeding only), adds the device to fs_devices->devices and alloc_list, increments num_devices, open_devices, rw_devices and total_devices, adds the device size to total_rw_bytes and free_chunk_space, may set rotating, increases the superblock total bytes and device count, clears the space info full flags and adds the sysfs device entry. For seeding it then calls init_first_rw_device under chunk_mutex. It then calls btrfs_add_dev_item and, for seeding, btrfs_finish_sprout and btrfs_sysfs_update_sprout_fsid. If init_first_rw_device, btrfs_add_dev_item or btrfs_finish_sprout fails, the transaction is aborted with that error and the rollback below is done. The first btrfs_commit_transaction is then called. Non-seeding case: its result ret is not rolled back on failure; the function goes on to btrfs_forget_devices(device->devt) and update_dev_time(device_path) and returns ret (0 on success, the commit error otherwise). Seeding case: uuid_mutex and s_umount are released right after the first commit; if that commit failed its error is returned at once (no rollback, no forget, no time update); otherwise btrfs_relocate_sys_chunks is called (its failure is only reported through btrfs_handle_fs_error and does not change the return value), then btrfs_attach_transaction: if that returns -ENOENT the function returns 0 immediately (skipping forget and time update); if it fails with another error it takes the rollback path with that error (the transaction handle is not ended again); else the second btrfs_commit_transaction result becomes ret, and the function then does btrfs_forget_devices and update_dev_time and returns ret. Rollback path (error_sysfs): removes the sysfs entry, takes device_list_mutex and chunk_mutex, unlinks the device from the lists, undoes the counters, free_chunk_space and superblock totals (restoring the saved original values), ends the transaction if one is held, destroys the zone info, frees the device, calls bdev_fput and releases uuid_mutex and s_umount only if still held; the error is returned.
note: Reviewer right: volumes.c btrfs_init_new_device ~3030-3047: uuid_mutex/s_umount are released right after the first commit, before btrfs_relocate_sys_chunks and the second commit; also failure rollbacks after the first commit, ENOENT return 0, and commit failure in non-seeding case not rolled back.

name: cachefiles_cull
prose: Function cachefiles_cull(cache, dir, filename): cull (unlink or bury) the named entry of directory dentry dir unless it is in use. Precondition: cache, dir and filename are valid; the caller does NOT hold the inode lock of dir (cachefiles_lookup_for_cull takes it, nested as parent). Postcondition: it first calls cachefiles_lookup_for_cull, which looks the name up with lookup_one while holding the inode lock of dir; if that returns an error, the function returns that error unchanged, the lock of dir already released and no dentry reference held. The lookup error values are: -ESTALE if lookup_one itself failed with -ENOENT; -ENOENT if the looked-up dentry is negative (nonexistent); -EBUSY if the victim inode already has S_KERNEL_FILE set; -ENOMEM if lookup_one failed with -ENOMEM; -EIO for lookup_one failing with -EIO (after cachefiles_io_error) or with any other error (after a pr_err). If the lookup succeeds, dir stays locked and the victim dentry reference is held. Then under the victim inode lock: if S_KERNEL_FILE is already set the internal result is -EBUSY, otherwise S_KERNEL_FILE is set on the victim inode. On the -EBUSY race, the inode lock of dir is released here, the victim reference is dropped and, since -EBUSY is neither -ENOENT nor -ENOMEM, pr_err is logged and -EIO is returned (not -EBUSY). Otherwise cachefiles_bury_object is called with dir locked (it releases the inode lock of dir itself on all its paths). On success fscache_count_culled is called, the victim reference is dropped and 0 is returned. On failure the victim reference is dropped, -ENOENT is turned into -ESTALE, -ENOMEM is returned as -ENOMEM, and any other error is logged with pr_err and returned as -EIO; S_KERNEL_FILE stays set on the victim in that case. On every return the inode lock of dir is released and no victim reference is held.
note: Reviewer right: namei.c cachefiles_lookup_for_cull: lookup_error converts -ENOENT->-ESTALE (l.~755), other lookup errors -> -EIO/-ENOMEM; negative dentry (lookup_put) gives -ENOENT, in-use gives -EBUSY; cull returns them unchanged.

name: EXTN_FEATURE_FUNCS(4)
prose: Generated function ext4_has_unknown_ext4_incompat_features(sb) (one of three inline functions defined by the macro invocation EXTN_FEATURE_FUNCS(4), with ver = 4). Precondition: sb is a valid ext4 super_block whose EXT4_SB(sb)->s_es superblock copy is valid and readable. Postcondition: returns true if and only if s_es->s_feature_incompat has at least one bit set outside EXT4_FEATURE_INCOMPAT_SUPP (the mask of incompat features this kernel supports; the test is (s_feature_incompat & cpu_to_le32(~EXT4_FEATURE_INCOMPAT_SUPP)) != 0), otherwise false; it modifies no state and takes no lock.

name: DEADLINE_DEBUGFS_DDIR_ATTRS(DD_RT_PRIO, DD_READ, read0)
prose: Generated function deadline_read0_fifo_start(m, pos). Precondition: m->private points to a valid request_queue whose q->elevator->elevator_data is the mq-deadline struct deadline_data dd, and pos is a valid pointer to the seq_file position. Postcondition: acquires dd->lock with spin_lock and returns, with the lock still held in every case (including a NULL result), seq_list_start(&dd->per_prio[DD_RT_PRIO].fifo_list[DD_READ], *pos): a pointer to the list_head node at index *pos of that FIFO list, or NULL if *pos is negative or is at or past the end of the list. The lock must later be released by deadline_read0_fifo_stop; no error code is returned and no memory is allocated.
note: mq-deadline.c DEADLINE_DEBUGFS_DDIR_ATTRS start: spin_lock(&dd->lock); return seq_list_start(&per_prio->fifo_list[data_dir], *pos); stop does spin_unlock. Verified.

name: aio_poll
prose: Precondition: aiocb is an initialised aio_kiocb (ki_ctx valid, poll.file set) and iocb is the kernel copy of the user control block for IOCB_CMD_POLL; the caller holds no ctx_lock. Postcondition: returns -EINVAL (before touching the poll request) if iocb->aio_buf has bits above the low 16, or aio_offset, aio_nbytes or aio_rw_flags is nonzero. Otherwise it initialises the poll request (events = demangle_poll(aio_buf) | EPOLLERR | EPOLLHUP), calls vfs_poll with a queueing callback, takes ctx->ctx_lock (irq-disabling) and returns apt.error, which is 0 or -EINVAL. Cases: (1) the file registered no waitqueue: if an event of the request was ready, ki_res.res = mangle_poll(mask), the iocb reference is dropped with iocb_put and 0 is returned (completed synchronously); if none was ready -EINVAL is returned and the caller keeps the iocb reference. (2) the file registered exactly one waitqueue (apt.error 0): if the request was already removed from the waitqueue, or aio_poll_wake already scheduled the completion work, an already-done or in-progress completion is assumed, mask is ignored and the function returns 0 (when the request is still on the queue with work scheduled, it is also added to ctx->active_reqs with ki_cancel = aio_poll_cancel; when it was removed from the queue nothing more is done); otherwise, if an event was ready, the wait entry is removed from the waitqueue, ki_res.res = mangle_poll(mask), the iocb reference is dropped and 0 is returned; otherwise the request is added to ctx->active_reqs with ki_cancel = aio_poll_cancel and 0 is returned. (3) the file registered more than one waitqueue (apt.error = -EINVAL): if the request was no longer on its first queue or completion work was already scheduled, req->cancelled is set and 0 is returned; otherwise (still on the first queue, no work scheduled) the wait entry is removed and, if an event was ready, the request is completed synchronously (ki_res.res = mangle_poll(mask), iocb_put, return 0), else -EINVAL is returned and the caller keeps the iocb reference. ctx_lock and the waitqueue lock are released before returning.
note: aio.c aio_poll l.~1900-1945: multi-queue case (apt.error=-EINVAL, queued) with an event ready (mask != 0, on_queue, no work) completes synchronously and returns 0, not -EINVAL; prose did not say mask must be 0. Rest verified.

name: __io_submit_one
prose: Precondition: req is a freshly allocated aio_kiocb belonging to ctx, iocb is the kernel copy of the user iocb, user_iocb its user address, compat the layout flag. Postcondition: returns -EBADF if fget(iocb->aio_fildes) fails (req->ki_filp is NULL, no reference taken); if IOCB_FLAG_RESFD is set and eventfd_ctx_fdget fails returns that error (PTR_ERR) with req->ki_filp holding a file reference; returns -EFAULT if writing KIOCB_KEY to user_iocb->aio_key fails (req->ki_filp, and req->ki_eventfd if set, hold references); otherwise it fills req->ki_res (obj, data, res = 0, res2 = 0) and returns the result of the handler for iocb->aio_lio_opcode: aio_read (PREAD, PREADV), aio_write (PWRITE, PWRITEV), aio_fsync (FSYNC with datasync false, FDSYNC with true) or aio_poll (POLL). Those handlers return 0 (the request completed or will be completed asynchronously) or a negative errno (they never return -EIOCBQUEUED to this function: aio_read and aio_write absorb it); any other opcode returns -EINVAL. This function does not itself release the file or eventfd references: they stay in req and are released when req is destroyed, which the caller (io_submit_one) does via iocb_destroy (and returns the slot with put_reqs_available) when the return value is nonzero; when the return is 0 the request is complete or will be completed asynchronously and the async machinery owns req and its references.
note: aio.c:1581-1650: aio_read/aio_write/aio_fsync never return -EIOCBQUEUED (aio_rw_done consumes it, they return 0 or errno); aio_poll returns 0/-EINVAL; io_submit_one at aio.c:2023-2064 does iocb_put then iocb_destroy+put_reqs_available on nonzero.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE3(io_cancel, aio_context_t, ctx_id, struct iocb __user *, iocb,
prose: Generated syscall sys_io_cancel(ctx_id, iocb, result). Precondition: iocb is a user pointer to a previously submitted control block; result is unused. Postcondition: returns -EFAULT if iocb->aio_key cannot be read, -EINVAL if the key is not KIOCB_KEY or lookup_ioctx(ctx_id) finds no context (no reference taken). Otherwise, under ctx->ctx_lock it searches ctx->active_reqs for the request whose ki_res.obj equals the iocb address; if found it calls its ki_cancel callback, removes it from the active list (list_del_init) and uses the callback's return; if not found the result stays -EINVAL. A callback return of 0 is converted to -EINPROGRESS (the completion event is delivered through the ring, not via result); any other callback return value (non-zero) is returned unchanged. The context reference is dropped before returning.
note: aio.c SYSCALL_DEFINE3(io_cancel) l.~2200-2240 verified: get_user->-EFAULT, key!=KIOCB_KEY->-EINVAL, lookup fail -EINVAL, ki_cancel under ctx_lock, 0->-EINPROGRESS, percpu_ref_put.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE6(io_pgetevents
prose: Generated syscall sys_io_pgetevents(ctx_id, min_nr, nr, events, timeout, usig). Precondition: events is a user buffer for up to nr io_events; timeout, if non-NULL, points to a user __kernel_timespec; usig, if non-NULL, points to a user __aio_sigset. Postcondition: returns -EFAULT if timeout cannot be copied or if usig cannot be copied; otherwise calls set_user_sigmask(ksig.sigmask, ksig.sigsetsize) (a NULL usig gives a NULL mask) and returns its non-zero error (e.g. -EINVAL for a wrong sigsetsize, -EFAULT) without waiting. On success of that it waits for events with do_io_getevents (result: number of events read, or -EINVAL for bad ctx_id or min_nr outside 0..nr, or a read_events error), then records whether a signal is pending and calls restore_saved_sigmask_unless(interrupted), which restores the caller's original signal mask unless a signal is pending (in which case it is restored on signal delivery). If interrupted and the result is 0 it returns -ERESTARTNOHAND; otherwise it returns the result.
note: aio.c io_pgetevents ~2283-2305 + set_user_sigmask (signal.c:3354) verified.

name: ceph_readdir
prose: Precondition: file is an open ceph directory file (file->private_data is its struct ceph_dir_file_info), ctx is a valid dir_context and the caller holds the inode lock of the directory for iteration as usual for iterate; no ceph spinlocks are held. Postcondition: returns 0 immediately if CEPH_F_ATEND is set. Otherwise it first emits "." (pos 0) and ".." (pos 1), advancing ctx->pos to 1 and 2; if dir_emit refuses one of them (caller buffer full) it returns 0 with ctx->pos left at that entry position. It then returns the negative errno of ceph_fscrypt_prepare_readdir if that fails (a positive return of it is ignored). It touches the write file mode under i_ceph_lock. If the dcache can be used (mount option DCACHE set, NOASYNCREADDIR not set, not a snapdir, directory complete and ordered, shared file cap issued) it calls __dcache_readdir and returns its result unless that is -EAGAIN, in which case it falls through. Normal path: when the buffered reply (dfi->last_readdir) does not cover ctx->pos it drops the previous reply and sends a READDIR (or LSSNAP) request to the auth MDS for the current frag, returning -errno on failure of request creation (PTR_ERR), reply-buffer allocation, kzalloc of r_path2 (-ENOMEM), encoding of the encrypted last name, or the request itself (in each case the request reference taken here is dropped), or the note_last_dentry error (after dropping the reply). The reply is then kept in dfi->last_readdir. It emits the buffered entries from ctx->pos onward, setting ctx->pos to each entry offset before dir_emit and incrementing it after a successful emit; it returns -EIO (after dropping the reply: dfi->last_readdir becomes NULL) if an entry offset is below ctx->pos or an entry has no inode; if dir_emit refuses an entry it returns 0 with ctx->pos at that entry offset and dfi->last_readdir retained (not dropped) so the next call resumes. When the buffered entries are exhausted the reply reference is dropped (last_readdir = NULL) and it moves on to further requests for the same frag or the next frag; at the end of the last frag it sets CEPH_F_ATEND and, if i_release_count still equals dfi->dir_release_count, marks the directory complete (and, only when dfi->dir_ordered_count also equals i_ordered_count, complete and ordered, setting i_size to the readdir-cache size), then returns 0. On every return no spinlock is held; a reply reference remains in dfi->last_readdir only if it was kept from an earlier request and not yet dropped (in particular after a full-buffer stop).
note: Reviewer wrong on both counts: dir.c:~606-619 offset<ctx->pos puts the reply, sets last_readdir NULL, returns -EIO; dir.c:~571-579 full buffer returns 0 WITHOUT putting last_readdir. Prose tightened only for i_size condition and last_readdir ownership (dir.c ~640-660).

name: __dir_lease_check
prose: Function __dir_lease_check(dentry, lwc) in ceph dir.c (static, returns one of KEEP = 0, DELETE = 1, TOUCH = 2, STOP = 4). Precondition: dentry is a ceph dentry whose d_lock is held by the caller (it is called from the lease walk), and lwc points to a walk control with dir_lease_ttl and expire_dir_lease set. Postcondition: let r = __dir_lease_try_check(dentry). That callee returns 0 without changing anything if di->lease_shared_gen is already 0 or the dentry is a root; otherwise it trylocks the i_ceph_lock of the parent inode and, if the trylock fails, returns -EBUSY without changing anything; if the lock is obtained it returns 1 when the parent i_shared_gen equals di->lease_shared_gen and CEPH_CAP_FILE_SHARED is issued, else 0 and sets di->lease_shared_gen to 0; the parent lock is released before it returns. If r == -EBUSY this function returns KEEP. If r > 0 (valid dir lease) it returns STOP if jiffies is still before di->time + lwc->dir_lease_ttl; else KEEP if lwc->expire_dir_lease is false; else TOUCH if dentry->d_lockref.count > 0 or CEPH_DENTRY_REFERENCED is set in di->flags; else it sets di->lease_shared_gen = 0 and returns DELETE. If r == 0 it returns DELETE (no expiry check). No lock or reference is acquired or retained, and the only field of the dentry state ever written is di->lease_shared_gen (by the callee when it found the lease invalid, or here on the final DELETE branch with a valid but expired lease).
note: Reviewer right: dir.c:1904-1931 __dir_lease_try_check zeroes lease_shared_gen only when valid==0 after the check; -EBUSY (trylock failed) and the early returns 0 (gen already 0, IS_ROOT) do not modify it.

name: resolve_indirect_refs
prose: Precondition: ctx, path and preftrees are valid; preftrees->indirect holds only indirect refs (none has ref->parent set); sc is NULL or a share-check context. Postcondition: allocates a local ulist of parents (returns -ENOMEM, nothing changed, if that fails). Then, while the indirect tree is not empty, it takes its first ref: if that ref has parent set (a bug) it warns and returns -EINVAL, leaving the ref in the indirect tree; otherwise it removes the ref from the indirect tree and decrements the tree count. A ref with count 0 is freed. If sc is set and the root_id of the ref differs from the root id of sc->root, the ref is freed and BACKREF_FOUND_SHARED (6, a positive value) is returned. Otherwise resolve_indirect_ref is called with the parents ulist. A result of -ENOENT is tolerated: the unresolved ref is inserted into the direct tree as is. Any other non-zero result (negative errno such as -ENOMEM, -EIO, -EUCLEAN, other tree search errors, or a positive value from the callee) frees the ref and is returned. On a zero result the ref itself receives the first parent of the ulist (0 if the ulist is empty) and that parent inode list; for every further parent a new prelim_ref is allocated (-ENOMEM after freeing the current ref if that fails), copied from the ref with its own parent and inode list, and inserted into the direct tree; the ref itself is inserted into the direct tree last (it may be merged or freed there). The ulist is then reinitialised (the inode lists now belong to the refs) and the loop goes on. Returns 0 if the whole indirect tree was consumed. On an early return the refs not yet taken stay in the indirect tree. On every return (success or failure) free_leaf_list frees the parents ulist and the inode lists attached to its nodes at that moment, including, after a failure part-way, lists already attached to refs inserted in the direct tree in the same iteration.
note: Reviewer wrong: backref.c:~786-810 first parent goes into the original ref, new refs only for further parents; error paths free_pref(ref) (l.~775,~798) and free_leaf_list(parents) at out frees inode lists. Prose tightened: WARN path leaves ref in tree, positive ret2 possible, BACKREF_FOUND_SHARED=6.

name: btrfs_finish_one_ordered
prose: Precondition: ordered_extent is a valid ordered extent whose IO has completed (data written or failed) and not yet completed here; the caller owns one reference and the ordered tree owns another. Postcondition: returns 0 on success and a negative errno on failure; the possible errors are -EIO when BTRFS_ORDERED_IOERR was already set, an error from btrfs_zone_finish_endio, from joining the transaction, from btrfs_insert_raid_extent, -EINVAL for a NOCOW ordered extent still linked on its csum list, or an error from btrfs_mark_extent_written, insert_ordered_extent_file_extent, btrfs_unpin_extent_cache, add_pending_csums or btrfs_update_inode_fallback. Steps: if the extent was truncated to length 0 it goes straight to the common exit with result 0 and nothing inserted. For a non-NOCOW extent (COW, PREALLOC, DIRECT or ENCODED) it locks the range (EXTENT_LOCKED | EXTENT_FINISHING_ORDERED) before joining a transaction (the free-space transaction join is used for a free-space inode). Once a transaction is joined, every failure aborts it (the early -EIO, zone-finish, truncated-to-zero and join-failure paths have no transaction to abort). Success for a NOCOW extent: after the raid-extent insert and the csum-list check it only writes the safe disk i_size and updates the inode item (btrfs_update_inode_fallback); no file extent item is inserted, no extent cache is unpinned and no checksums are added. Success for a non-NOCOW extent: for a PREALLOC extent the range is marked written (btrfs_mark_extent_written), otherwise the file extent item is inserted (and the reserved extent is considered consumed, the delalloc bytes of the block group are released); then the extent cache is unpinned, pending checksums are added, EXTENT_DELALLOC_NEW | EXTENT_ADD_INODE_BYTES is cleared for the range when applicable (not DIRECT/ENCODED/PREALLOC and not truncated), the safe disk i_size is written and the inode item is updated. Common exit: the extent bits of the range (EXTENT_DEFRAG, plus LOCKED and FINISHING_ORDERED when they were taken and DELALLOC_NEW where it applies) are cleared and the transaction, if any, is ended. Then, if the result is non-zero or the extent was truncated: on failure BTRFS_ORDERED_IOERR is set on the ordered extent (btrfs_mark_ordered_extent_error); the extent map range not written (the whole range, or the part after the truncated length) is dropped unless the inode is a free-space inode; and when (failure or truncated to length 0), the file extent was not already inserted and the ordered extent is neither NOCOW nor PREALLOC, the reserved extent is returned to the allocator (discarded first if the discard=sync option is on and it failed) and the data qgroup reservation is freed. In every case, even on failure, the ordered extent is removed from the inode and root lists, remaining bio cs lists are cleaned up, and both references (the tree and the caller) are dropped, so the caller must not use ordered_extent afterwards.
note: Reviewer right: inode.c btrfs_finish_one_ordered NOCOW branch (~3223-3240) writes only disk i_size + inode update then goto out; skips extent insert/unpin/csums/DELALLOC_NEW clearing.

name: coda_waitfor_upcall
prose: Precondition: vcp and req are valid, the caller holds vcp->vc_mutex, req was queued by coda_upcall on vcp->vc_pending (it may meanwhile have been moved to the processing list; req->uc_chain is on one of the two lists) and req->uc_sleep is initialised. Postcondition: returns void and vcp->vc_mutex is held again on return (it is dropped around every sleep and retaken afterwards). On entry the current signal mask is saved and every signal except SIGKILL, SIGSTOP and SIGINT is blocked (coda_block_signals), a wait-queue entry for the current task is added to req->uc_sleep, and the deadline is jiffies + coda_timeout seconds. It then loops: it sets the task state to TASK_INTERRUPTIBLE if CODA_INTERRUPTIBLE(req) holds (coda_hard is 0 and the opcode is not CLOSE, STORE, ACCESS_INTENT or RELEASE, or CODA_REQ_READ is set) and to TASK_UNINTERRUPTIBLE otherwise. If req->uc_flags has CODA_REQ_WRITE or CODA_REQ_ABORT set (a reply or abort arrived) the loop ends without touching the lists. Otherwise, if the mask is still blocked, the deadline has passed and the request is interruptible, the saved mask is restored (once). If signal_pending(current) is then true (this can be due to an unblocked SIGKILL, SIGSTOP or SIGINT even before the deadline, whether or not the request is interruptible, or to any signal once the mask is restored) req is removed from its list with list_del(&req->uc_chain) and the loop ends. Otherwise vc_mutex is released, the task sleeps (schedule_timeout of one second while the mask is still blocked, schedule() once it is restored) and vc_mutex is retaken. After the loop, if the mask is still blocked it is restored; the wait-queue entry is removed and the task state is set to TASK_RUNNING. There is no return value: why the wait ended is visible only in req->uc_flags and signal_pending(current). Nothing is freed.
note: coda_waitfor_upcall: upcall.c loop; list_del only on signal; signal_pending check not gated on the timeout, so a pending unblocked signal ends the wait early.

name: lookup_zone
prose: Precondition: dm points to a valid struct adfs_discmap whose dm_bh->b_data holds the zone's map bytes (every bit position read must have at least 4 readable bytes, because each fragment id is read with a 32-bit unaligned load), dm_startbit and dm_endbit delimit the fragment area of the zone, idlen is the fragment id length in bits with 1 <= idlen <= 19 (the limit of the ADFS map format, enforced at mount; the 32-bit load only yields correct ids up to 25 bits), frag_id is the id searched for, and offset points to a writable unsigned int holding the bit offset to find among the fragments whose id equals frag_id. Postcondition: it first reads the free-space link at bit 8 of the zone (id masked to 15 bits and idlen bits); 0 means no free fragment, otherwise the first free fragment is at bit 8 + that value. It then scans fragments starting at dm_startbit (the loop body always runs at least once): the id of the fragment (idlen bits) is read and its last bit is the next set bit at or after start + idlen; if that bit is at or beyond dm_endbit an "adfs: oversized fragment" error is logged and -1 is returned (with *offset already reduced by the matching fragments skipped so far). A fragment that starts at the current free-link position is a free-space fragment: it is skipped, never matched, and the free link advances by its id value masked with 0x7fff. Any other fragment whose id equals frag_id has length L = last bit + 1 - start; if *offset < L the function returns start + *offset (the map bit holding that offset) and *offset is left at the original value minus the lengths of the matching fragments skipped before it; otherwise *offset is decreased by L. The scan continues at last bit + 1 while that is below dm_endbit. If the scan runs off the end of the zone it returns -1 and *offset has been reduced by the total length of all matching fragments (the original *offset was at least that total). A frag_id with bits set above idlen never matches. No lock or reference is acquired or released and nothing else is modified.
note: Reviewer right that idlen up to 31 is not what the code supports: map.c comment "limited to 19 bits by F+ version 2" and super.c:81-82 (max_idlen 19); GET_FRAG_ID uses a 32-bit load shifted by up to 7. Contract dropped (none present). Added the free-link read at bit 8 and the oversized-fragment error path.

name: _badblocks_set
prose: Precondition: bb points to an initialized struct badblocks whose page table is valid; the caller must not hold bb->lock (the function takes the write seqlock itself with interrupts saved); s and sectors give the range and acknowledged says whether new entries are acknowledged. Postcondition: returns false, without taking the lock or changing anything, if bb->shift < 0 (badblocks disabled) or sectors == 0. Otherwise (note the rounddown/roundup calls under bb->shift are statement expressions whose results are discarded, so s and sectors are NOT rounded) it takes the write seqlock and repeatedly inserts, merges, combines or overwrites entries for [s, s+sectors), advancing s and shrinking sectors by the length handled each pass (a pass may also skip over a range that is already recorded with ack state that cannot be overwritten). It stops early, with only part of the range (possibly none) recorded, when the table is full or when a front overwrite would need extra table slots (extra > 0) that cannot be had; it then returns false. If the whole range is processed it also tries to combine with the following entry (try_adjacent_combine) and returns true. The return value is exactly (remaining sectors == 0). If at least one entry was added or merged (added != 0) it calls set_changed(bb) and, if acknowledged is 0, sets bb->unacked_exist = 1, else calls badblocks_update_acked(bb). bb->count is updated for every insertion, combine or overwrite. The write seqlock is released (interrupt flags restored) on every path that took it.
note: rounddown/roundup in this tree are statement-expression macros that return a value and do not assign (include/linux/math.h:71-90); the calls at block/badblocks.c:860-861 discard the result, so s, next and sectors are unchanged (sectors = next - s = sectors). Prose verified against the rest of _badblocks_set (badblocks.c:852-979).

name: create_elf_fdpic_tables
prose: Real function create_elf_fdpic_tables(bprm, mm, exec_params, interp_params) in fs/binfmt_elf_fdpic.c (the head is in the previous slice, so the name is not in this slice; the earlier name create_elf_fdpic_stack_layout does not exist). Precondition: bprm, mm, exec_params and interp_params are valid, exec_params->loadmap is populated, interp_params->loadmap is NULL or populated, and the argument strings (bprm->argc of them) followed by the environment strings (bprm->envc) were already pushed by exec so that they start at the user address arg_start (bprm->p on MMU; start_stack - (MAX_ARG_PAGES * PAGE_SIZE - bprm->p) without MMU). Postcondition: returns 0 after writing onto the user stack, from the top: the ELF_PLATFORM and ELF_BASE_PLATFORM strings if the architecture defines them, the exec load map and, if interp_params->loadmap is non-NULL, the interpreter load map, the auxiliary vector, the NULL-terminated envp[] and argv[] pointer arrays and argc; and after setting exec_params->map_addr, interp_params->map_addr (only if an interpreter load map exists), current->mm->context.exec_fdpic_loadmap and interp_fdpic_loadmap (the latter only if present), the auxiliary vector copy in mm->saved_auxv, mm->arg_start, arg_end, env_start, env_end and finally mm->start_stack = the final 16-byte-aligned stack pointer. Returns -EFAULT if transfer_args_to_stack fails (non-MMU), if any copy_to_user fails, or if any put_user of an argv[]/envp[] entry, a terminating NULL or argc fails. Returns -EINVAL if, while filling argv[] or envp[], strnlen_user returns 0 (the string cannot be read) or a length greater than MAX_ARG_STRLEN (no terminating NUL within that limit); an empty string (length 1) is accepted and causes no error. An internal consistency check BUG_ON(csp != sp) halts the kernel if the computed stack layout is inconsistent. On failure the user stack and some mm and params fields may be partly updated (for example map_addr is set before the load map is copied); no lock or reference is acquired and nothing is freed.
note: Reviewer right: strnlen_user returns the length including the NUL (1 for an empty string), 0 only on fault, > count if too long (binfmt_elf_fdpic.c:711-713 and 725-727); the old text claimed empty strings give -EINVAL. Name create_elf_fdpic_tables confirmed at binfmt_elf_fdpic.c:500.

name: exfat_get_block
prose: Precondition: inode is a valid exfat inode, bh_result is a buffer_head whose b_size is the requested mapping length in bytes (a positive multiple of the block size) and whose b_folio may be NULL (direct I/O), iblock is the file-relative block, create is 0 or 1, and the caller does not hold sbi->s_lock (it is taken and released exactly once here). Postcondition: returns 0 or a negative errno. With s_lock held it reads i_size. If iblock >= last_block (i_size rounded up to blocks) and create is 0, or exfat_map_cluster returns EXFAT_EOF_CLUSTER, it goes to the common exit with max_blocks equal to the requested block count, bh_result is not mapped by this function (its flags are left as they were) and the result is 0. If exfat_map_cluster fails it returns that errno at once (an fs error is logged unless it is -ENOSPC) with bh_result (b_size and flags) untouched. Otherwise the block is mapped with map_bh (a delay flag is cleared) and max_blocks is limited to the rest of the cluster. Let valid_blks be valid_size in blocks, rounded up if i_size == valid_size, create is set or there is no folio, else rounded down. If iblock + max_blocks < valid_blks the range is mapped as is. Otherwise, if iblock < valid_blks, max_blocks is reduced to valid_blks - iblock (only the written part is mapped) and the buffer stays mapped. Otherwise, if create is set, the buffer is marked new, ei->valid_size is set to the end of the range (iblock + max_blocks blocks, in bytes) and the inode is marked dirty. Otherwise, for a folio-backed read of the single block at iblock == valid_blks when valid_size is not block aligned, max_blocks becomes 1 and: -EAGAIN if the folio has no buffers, -EINVAL (with an fs error message) if bh_result->b_data differs from the expected address in the folio, the error of bh_read if the read fails, otherwise the block is read and its part beyond valid_size is zeroed (result 0). In every other non-create case beyond valid_size the mapped flag is cleared (the range reads as zeros) and max_blocks is not reduced. At the common exit b_size is set to max_blocks blocks in bytes and, if the result is negative, the mapped flag is cleared (so on the -EAGAIN, -EINVAL and bh_read-error paths b_size is one block and the buffer is unmapped). Thus b_size is bounded by the requested size and the cluster end, is cut to the written part when the range straddles valid_size, and is not cut when the range lies wholly beyond valid_size. s_lock is released on every path.
note: Reviewer right: inode.c "The range has been partially written" branch sets max_blocks = valid_blks - iblock before done; old prose's last sentence said b_size was not reduced in that case (and contradicted its own earlier text).

name: EXT4_FEATURE_COMPAT_FUNCS(journal,		HAS_JOURNAL)
prose: Generated function ext4_set_feature_journal(sb) (defined by the macro invocation EXT4_FEATURE_COMPAT_FUNCS(journal, HAS_JOURNAL)). Precondition: sb is a valid ext4 super_block whose EXT4_SB(sb)->s_es superblock copy is valid and writable. Postcondition: first calls ext4_update_dynamic_rev(sb) (which may raise s_es->s_rev_level to the dynamic revision and initialise the related fields), then ORs EXT4_FEATURE_COMPAT_HAS_JOURNAL (0x0004) into s_es->s_feature_compat leaving all other bits unchanged; returns nothing. It does not mark the superblock buffer dirty, takes no lock and no reference.
note: Verified against ext4.h EXT4_FEATURE_COMPAT_FUNCS: set = ext4_update_dynamic_rev(sb) then s_feature_compat |= cpu_to_le32(0x0004); no dirty marking, no lock, void.

name: create_pending_snapshot
prose: Precondition: trans is a running transaction handle in the commit phase, pending is an initialised pending-snapshot descriptor with non-NULL path and root_item (both asserted), and root, dir, dentry and readonly describe the source subvolume, parent directory and new name. Postcondition: the function always clears the pending state before returning: new_root_item is freed, pending->root_item and pending->path are set to NULL (the path is freed by its scope-based cleanup), the filename is freed if it was set up, and the skip-qgroup mark is cleared once it was set. Early failures (fscrypt_setup_filename, btrfs_get_free_objectid, reservation of the relocation metadata with btrfs_block_rsv_add when it is needed) store the errno in pending->error and return 0 (ret is still 0 at that point); an existing directory entry of the same name stores -EEXIST in pending->error and returns 0 after restoring trans->block_rsv and clearing trans->bytes_reserved. Otherwise it switches trans->block_rsv to the pending reservation and performs the snapshot: records the parent root in the transaction (a failure here is returned without aborting the transaction), picks the directory index, checks that the name does not exist, creates the qgroup (-EEXIST, and -ENOTCONN when quotas are disabled, are ignored), runs the delayed items, records the source root in the transaction, sets last_snapshot, copies the root item (readonly flag per pending->readonly, new uuid, parent uuid, otime), COWs and copies the root node, inserts the new root item and root ref, gets the new fs root into pending->snap, does the relocation and qgroup accounting, inserts the directory item, updates the parent inode and adds the subvolume uuid and, if present, the received uuid to the uuid tree (-EOVERFLOW on the received-uuid insertion is turned into 0). On a failure after the reservation switch it sets pending->error to the errno and returns it; every such failure aborts the transaction except the failure to record the parent root, the qgroup accounting/inherit step and an -EEXIST from the received-uuid insertion, which are returned (and stored in pending->error) without an abort. On success it returns 0 and pending->error is 0. On all paths after the switch trans->block_rsv is restored and trans->bytes_reserved is cleared; pending->snap is not released here and stays set once btrfs_get_new_fs_root succeeded.
note: Reviewer wrong: ret is initialised to 0 and the early failures only set pending->error, so they return 0; the path is declared BTRFS_PATH_AUTO_FREE so it is freed at return, and pending->path = NULL at the end. Small additions: -EEXIST from btrfs_create_qgroup is ignored, and the record_root_in_trans(parent) failure and qgroup failures do not abort.

name: btrfs_commit_transaction
prose: Precondition: trans is the only user of its handle (use_count == 1) for the running transaction cur_trans = trans->transaction of trans->fs_info and the caller holds no transaction-related lock; the caller must not use trans afterwards, since every path ends or frees the handle. Postcondition: it first clears BTRFS_FS_NEED_TRANS_COMMIT. (1) If the transaction is already aborted it ends the handle with btrfs_end_transaction and returns the abort error. Otherwise it releases the handle's reserved metadata and sets trans->block_rsv to NULL; if no other task is already flushing it runs the delayed refs once (btrfs_run_delayed_refs(trans, 0)); it creates the pending block groups (result ignored); and, if no task has done so yet, starts the dirty block groups. If the delayed refs run or the dirty block group start fails it ends the handle with btrfs_end_transaction and returns that negative errno, without cleaning up the transaction. (2) Then, under trans_lock, if cur_trans->state is already at least COMMIT_PREP (another task is committing) it links the pending snapshot of trans, if any, into cur_trans->pending_snapshots (add_pending_snapshot), takes an extra transaction reference, ends the handle, waits until the commit is COMPLETED (SUPER_COMMITTED for an fsync) and returns the transaction's abort error if it aborted, otherwise the result of btrfs_end_transaction (the extra reference is put). (3) Otherwise this task performs the commit: it sets state COMMIT_PREP; waits for a previous transaction that has not reached the wanted state and fails with that transaction's abort error, or with -EROFS if there is no previous transaction in the list and the filesystem is in an error state; sets COMMIT_START; starts the delalloc flush (always 0), runs the delayed items, waits until there are no external writers, runs the delayed items again, waits for the delalloc flush and for pending ordered extents; pauses scrub; under trans_lock it links the pending snapshot (add_pending_snapshot) and sets COMMIT_DOING; waits until it is the only writer, and fails with the abort error if the transaction is aborted; then holding reloc_mutex it creates the pending snapshots, runs the delayed items and all delayed refs, commits the fs roots, frees the log root tree, accounts qgroup extents, commits the cow-only roots, fails with the abort error if aborted, switches the commit roots, updates the super block copy, sets UNBLOCKED and fs_info->running_transaction to NULL, writes the btree pages and waits for them (a failure is also reported with btrfs_handle_fs_error), writes all superblocks, sets SUPER_COMMITTED, finishes the extent commit, sets the last committed transid and the state COMPLETED, removes the transaction from the list, drops two transaction references, frees the handle, resumes scrub and returns 0. If any step of (3) fails, the cleanup path releases the metadata and the pending block groups, detaches the handle from the task, logs the warning "Skipping commit of aborted transaction" and cleanup_transaction aborts the transaction with the errno, removes and destroys it, drops its references and frees the handle; the negative errno is returned. A pending snapshot attached to trans is therefore linked into the transaction only when the function reaches add_pending_snapshot in (2) or in (3); it is not linked on the failure paths of (1) nor on failures in (3) that happen before COMMIT_DOING (previous transaction aborted, -EROFS, delayed items).
note: Reviewer's specific claim wrong (the early-return branch does call add_pending_snapshot, transaction.c:2280) but the old prose's "in every case ... linked" was false: the abort / delayed-refs / dirty-bg paths (label lockdep_trans_commit_start_release) and the pre-COMMIT_DOING failures never call it; add_pending_snapshot is called only at 2280 and 2393.

name: crypto_register_alg
prose: Precondition: alg is a fully set-up struct crypto_alg that is not yet registered; the caller may sleep (kmemdup with GFP_KERNEL, down_write(&crypto_alg_sem)). Postcondition: it first clears CRYPTO_ALG_DEAD in alg->cra_flags (this happens even if the next check fails). crypto_check_alg then fails with -EINVAL for an empty cra_name or cra_driver_name, an alignmask that is not of the form 2^n - 1 or exceeds MAX_ALGAPI_ALIGNMASK, a blocksize above MAX_ALGAPI_BLOCKSIZE, a type-less CRYPTO_ALG_TYPE_CIPHER above the cipher limits, or a negative priority; crypto_register_alg returns that error, registers nothing, drops no reference and leaves cra_refcnt unset: the only change is the cleared DEAD flag (the module signature check inside crypto_check_alg may also panic in FIPS mode). Otherwise crypto_check_alg sets cra_refcnt to 1, the registration's reference. If CRYPTO_ALG_DUP_FIRST is set and cra_destroy is NULL, a kmemdup copy of the algorithm and its type-specific part is registered instead (with cra_destroy = crypto_free_alg); if that allocation fails it returns -ENOMEM with nothing registered. Under the crypto_alg_sem write lock it then calls __crypto_register_alg, which fails with -EAGAIN if the alg is dead, -EEXIST if the alg is already on the list or its names clash with a non-moribund registered algorithm or test larval, or with the error of crypto_alloc_test_larval (-ENOMEM, or -ENOENT if a module reference on alg cannot be taken); on any such failure the reference on alg is dropped with crypto_alg_put (which destroys a duplicated copy) and the negative errno is returned, nothing registered. On success the alg is on crypto_alg_list and 0 is returned. If no self-test is needed (CONFIG_CRYPTO_SELFTESTS off or CRYPTO_ALG_INTERNAL set) CRYPTO_ALG_TESTED is set and registration is finished at once: template instances that depend on same-named registered algorithms of lower or equal priority, or with the same driver name, are removed (crypto_remove_spawns), a CRYPTO_MSG_ALG_LOADED notification is sent, and the list of algorithms to put is released with crypto_remove_final. Otherwise a test larval is added, CRYPTO_ALG_TESTED is cleared and, if the boot self-tests are finished (crypto_boot_test_finished), the test is scheduled with crypto_schedule_test; if not, the (empty) put list is released and the test is left for later.
note: Reviewer right: algapi.c crypto_register_alg clears CRYPTO_ALG_DEAD before crypto_check_alg. Also corrected the 'replacing lower-priority algorithms' claim: crypto_alg_finish_registration (algapi.c:245-271) removes dependent template instances (crypto_remove_spawns), not the algorithms themselves.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE5(io_getevents_time32, __u32, ctx_id,
prose: Generated syscall sys_io_getevents_time32(ctx_id, min_nr, nr, events, timeout) (CONFIG_COMPAT_32BIT_TIME). Precondition: timeout, if non-NULL, points to a user struct old_timespec32 (relative). Postcondition: returns -EFAULT if timeout is non-NULL and cannot be copied; otherwise the result of do_io_getevents (events copied: 0 or fewer than min_nr on timeout, -EINVAL for an invalid context or min_nr outside 0..nr, or a read_events error), stored in an int, with a result of 0 replaced by -EINTR when a signal is pending.
note: Verified against aio.c:2349-2365 (get_old_timespec32 failure -> -EFAULT; do_io_getevents at 2218-2235 returns -EINVAL for no ctx or min_nr outside 0..nr; -EINTR substituted when ret == 0 and a signal is pending).

name: cachefiles_daemon_bind
prose: Precondition: cache points to a cachefiles_cache holding the configuration set so far (run, cull and stop percentages for files and blocks, rootdirname and tag, which may be NULL) and args points to the NUL-terminated argument string of the bind command. Postcondition: returns -ERANGE, changing nothing, if the file thresholds do not satisfy fstop < fcull < frun < 100 or the block thresholds do not satisfy bstop < bcull < brun < 100; -EINVAL (with a message) if rootdirname is NULL; -EBUSY (with a message) if CACHEFILES_READY is already set. With CONFIG_CACHEFILES_ONDEMAND enabled, an args string equal to "ondemand" sets CACHEFILES_ONDEMAND_MODE in cache->flags, an empty args string is accepted, and any other args returns -EINVAL before the flag is touched by this call; without that option any non-empty args returns -EINVAL. If cache->tag is NULL it is set to a kstrdup copy of "CacheFiles" (-ENOMEM if that fails; the tag is deliberately not freed on error because the release handler frees it). Otherwise it returns the result of cachefiles_add_cache(cache), 0 meaning the cache is now bound and ready. The CACHEFILES_ONDEMAND_MODE flag is set only on the "ondemand" path of this call, and it stays set if a later step fails (-ENOMEM from the tag allocation or an error from cachefiles_add_cache). No lock is taken or released here.
note: Reviewer right: daemon.c:782-792 returns -EINVAL for other non-empty args without calling set_bit; the old sentence implied the flag may be set on that return.

name: btrfs_split_extent_map
prose: Real function btrfs_split_extent_map(inode, start, len, pre, new_logical) in fs/btrfs/extent_map.c (the slice starts after the head, so the name is not in the slice). Precondition: 0 < pre < len; the inode's extent map tree holds an uncompressed, non-logging extent map of length len that overlaps [start, start + len), has a real disk_bytenr, is PINNED and is on the inode's modified extents list (its list head is not empty); these conditions are asserted; the caller holds neither the io_tree extent lock on that range nor em_tree->lock and holds no reference of its own on that map. Postcondition: returns -ENOMEM, with nothing locked or changed, if either of the two new extent maps cannot be allocated; otherwise it locks the range [start, start + len) in inode->io_tree, takes em_tree->lock for writing and looks the map up; if no extent map is found it returns -EIO leaving the tree unchanged. On success it returns 0 after replacing the old map by two maps that carry the old map's flags (including PINNED, captured before the flag is cleared on the old map) and generation and are inserted as modified: [em->start, em->start + pre) mapped to new_logical, and [em->start + pre, em->start + len) mapped to the old map's block start plus pre (the results of replace_extent_mapping and add_extent_mapping are not checked). The reference taken by the lookup inside this function and the tree's reference on the old map are dropped. In every case after the lock was taken it releases the write lock and the range lock, and it frees the references on any new extent map not inserted.
note: Reviewer right: ASSERT(!list_empty(&em->list)) at extent_map.c:1070 was omitted. Also corrected "caller's lookup reference": the "Once for us" reference is the one taken by btrfs_lookup_extent_mapping in this function.

name: replay_one_extent
prose: Precondition: wc->trans is a running transaction, wc->root is the subvolume root being replayed with a log root, wc->log_leaf, wc->log_slot and wc->log_key identify an EXTENT_DATA item in the log tree, and wc->subvol_path is released on entry. Postcondition: for an extent type other than REG, PREALLOC or INLINE it aborts the log replay and returns -EUCLEAN; if the inode cannot be read (btrfs_iget_logging) it aborts the replay and returns that error. Otherwise, if the subvolume already has an identical REG/PREALLOC file extent item at the same offset, it does nothing more and returns 0 (a negative result of the initial btrfs_lookup_file_extent is not checked: it is treated like "not found"). Else it drops the extents overlapping [start, extent_end) (extent_end = start + num_bytes, or the sector-aligned end for an inline extent) with btrfs_drop_extents; an inline extent is then overwritten with overwrite_item; a hole with the NO_HOLES feature is only accounted; for other items the file extent item is inserted into the subvolume tree, an explicit hole needs nothing more, and a real extent is qgroup-traced, then either referenced (btrfs_inc_extent_ref) if it already exists in the extent tree or allocated (btrfs_alloc_logged_file_extent) if not, and the checksums covering it are read from the log root, the existing checksums of that range are deleted from the csum tree and the logged ones added. Finally the file extent range [start, extent_end) is recorded in the inode, the inode byte count is updated by the extent size and the dropped bytes, and the inode item is updated. It returns 0 on success, or the negative errno of the failing step, each of which also aborts the log replay with a message (overwrite_item aborts internally before returning its error). The inode reference taken is dropped (iput) on every return after it was obtained, and the temporary checksum list is freed.
note: Reviewer wrong: overwrite_item itself calls btrfs_abort_log_replay on every failing path (tree-log.c overwrite_item: search_slot failure, -ENOMEM, insert failure), and replay_one_extent aborts on all other failing steps; the call at tree-log.c:812 returns that error without a second abort.

name: log_dir_items
prose: Precondition: trans is a running transaction handle, inode is a directory inode whose root has a log root, path and dst_path are unused paths, ctx is the log context, min_offset is the first dir index offset to consider and last_offset_ret is a writable u64 pointer. Postcondition: the function keeps last_old_dentry_offset (initially min_offset - 1) and last_offset (initially (u64)-1). It looks for the first leaf at or after the key (ino, DIR_INDEX, min_offset) whose generation is at least trans->transid (btrfs_search_forward; an error from that call is not reported but treated like "nothing found"). If none is found, or the key found is not a DIR_INDEX key of this directory, it searches for the last DIR_INDEX key of the directory (a btrfs_search_slot failure releases path and returns its negative errno at once, without releasing dst_path), sets last_old_dentry_offset to that key's offset if there is one (a negative btrfs_previous_item result ends with that error), and finishes with last_offset = (u64)-1. Otherwise it sets last_old_dentry_offset to the offset of the dir index key just before that first key if there is one (a negative btrfs_previous_item result ends with that error), re-finds the first key with btrfs_search_slot (taking the next item if it is gone; if no keys remain it finishes) and loops over leaves calling process_dir_items_leaf, which logs the DIR_INDEX items whose transid is the current one and whose offset is above inode->last_dir_index_offset (in batches), skips items of earlier transactions and already logged items, inserts a DIR_LOG_INDEX range key for each gap before a skipped old item, sets last_old_dentry_offset to the offset of each skipped old item, may set ctx->log_new_dentries and may allocate or reuse ctx->scratch_eb. The loop ends with last_offset = (u64)-1 when that function reports that it reached the last item (a positive result, turned into 0) or when there is no next leaf or the next leaf has no more dir index keys of this directory, and with last_offset = (that next key's offset) - 1 when the next leaf was not changed in this transaction; if rescheduling is needed it releases the path and restarts the search. At the common end path and dst_path are released. If the result so far is 0, *last_offset_ret is set to last_offset and, if last_old_dentry_offset < last_offset, one DIR_LOG_INDEX range key covering [last_old_dentry_offset + 1, last_offset] is inserted with insert_dir_log_key, whose error is the result. The return value is 0 or the negative errno of btrfs_search_slot, btrfs_previous_item, btrfs_next_item, btrfs_next_leaf, process_dir_items_leaf or insert_dir_log_key. On a failure before the final step *last_offset_ret is not written; if insert_dir_log_key fails it has already been written (to last_offset, the end of the covered range).
note: Reviewer right on both points: last_old_dentry_offset is updated to each skipped old dentry's key offset (tree-log.c process_dir_items_leaf, "*last_old_dentry_offset = key.offset") so it is not simply the key before the first logged one, and *last_offset_ret = last_offset is assigned before insert_dir_log_key at the done label. Also the old text said every item is logged (items older than trans or already logged are skipped) and omitted that btrfs_search_forward errors are swallowed.

name: btrfs_get_old_root
prose: Precondition: root is a btrfs root and time_seq is a sequence number registered with the tree modification log. Postcondition: it read-locks the current root node and takes a reference on it (btrfs_read_lock_root_node). If tree_mod_log_oldest_root finds no root modification at or after time_seq it returns that very node, still read-locked and referenced, and the caller owns both. Otherwise the current root node is read-unlocked and its reference dropped in every remaining case, and a different extent buffer eb is built: if the oldest relevant modification is a root replacement and tree_mod_log_search finds a log entry for the old root's logical address that is not a KEY_REMOVE_WHILE_FREEING entry, the old root block is read from disk (a read error or a not up-to-date block is logged with WARN_ON and a warning and NULL is returned), read-locked, cloned, unlocked and released, the log is searched again and NULL is returned if the later entry is missing or older than the first (the clone is freed); if the root was replaced but there is no such entry, a dummy extent buffer at the old root's logical address is allocated; if the root was not replaced, the current root node is cloned. NULL is returned if a clone or the allocation fails. For a replaced root the header of eb is set to bytenr = eb->start, backref revision MIXED, the level of the old root and the generation of the replace entry, and the owner is the owner of the current root node only in the dummy-buffer case and 0 in the read-old-block case. eb is then read-locked and, if a log entry was found, the operations after time_seq are rewound on it with tree_mod_log_rewind (if none was found it only warns when the level is not 0). The caller must btrfs_tree_read_unlock and free_extent_buffer a non-NULL result; on NULL no lock or reference taken by this function remains held.
note: Checked against tree-mod-log.c:1007-1085; only the owner/rewind details of the old text were imprecise.

name: write_folio_nounlock
prose: Precondition: folio is a locked folio of a ceph inode's mapping. wbc must be non-NULL on every path that calls folio_redirty_for_writepage before the request has completed (the not-writeable noop, the request creation failure and the bounce-page failure), because that function dereferences wbc; a NULL wbc is replaced by an uninitialised local writeback_control only after the OSD request finished with an error. Postcondition: the folio is never unlocked by this function. Returns -EIO at once if the inode is shut down. Returns 0 doing nothing else if the folio has no snap context. If the folio's snap context seq is greater than the oldest writeable context's seq it WARNs unless the caller is in PF_MEMALLOC, drops the oldest-context reference, redirties the folio and returns 0. If the folio position is at or beyond the inode size recorded in the writeback ctl it invalidates the whole folio (folio_invalidate) and returns 0 without writing. Otherwise it clips the length to i_size (the write length is rounded up to the fscrypt block size for encrypted inodes), increments fsc->writeback_count (setting write_congested above the threshold) and creates an OSD write request; if that fails it redirties the folio, decrements the count (clearing write_congested below the low threshold) and returns PTR_ERR(req). It then starts folio writeback (and the fscache write if caching is enabled); if the inode is encrypted and encrypting the page cache blocks fails it redirties the folio, ends writeback, puts the request, decrements the count and returns that error. Otherwise it attaches the page (or bounce page), starts the request and waits for it, updates the write metrics, frees the bounce page and puts the request; the result is the bytes written (>= 0, replaced by 0) or a negative error. On -ERESTARTSYS it redirties the folio (substituting the local wbc if wbc is NULL), ends writeback, decrements the count and returns -ERESTARTSYS, leaving the page's snap context attached. On any other negative error it sets fsc->blocklisted if the error is -EBLOCKLISTED, sets the mapping error and increments wbc->pages_skipped (the local wbc if NULL). On success and on those other errors it then detaches the folio's private snap context, ends writeback, drops the cap wrbuffer reference and the page's snap-context reference, decrements the count (clearing write_congested below the low threshold) and returns 0 on success or the negative error.
note: Reviewer partly right: the substitution exists only in the err<0 branch (addr.c:837-840); the three earlier redirty calls (in this function) use wbc directly and folio_redirty_for_writepage dereferences it (mm/page-writeback.c:2777). Callers pass NULL at addr.c:1857.

name: affs_write_end_ofs
prose: Real function: write_end for the OFS (old file system) address space; it copies the first len bytes of the page data at in-page offset pos & (PAGE_SIZE - 1) into the file chain of OFS data blocks (copied is ignored). Precondition: folio is locked, uptodate and holds the data of the write, referenced by the caller; mapping->host is an OFS inode; the caller does not use folio afterwards because this function unlocks it and drops the reference. Postcondition: the data is written block by block: a leading partial block (when the position is not block aligned) is read with affs_bread_ino and updated in place (its size field raised to cover the data, checksum fixed, buffer dirtied); then each whole block is obtained with affs_getemptyblk_ino and filled; then a trailing partial block is read or created with affs_bread_ino; for newly created blocks the data header is initialised (type, key, sequence, size, next) and linked from the previous block next pointer. If the first block cannot be read (the leading partial block, or the block before a block-aligned position) it returns that negative errno with nothing written (and the folio unlocked and put). Otherwise it marks the folio uptodate (unless an error occurred), releases the block buffer, extends inode->i_size and mmu_private to the end of the written data if larger, clears the FIBF_ARCHIVED protection bit (marking the inode dirty) if set, unlocks and puts the folio, and returns the number of bytes written. If allocating or reading a later block fails after some bytes were written it returns the bytes written so far; if nothing was written yet it returns PTR_ERR of the previous block buffer pointer: 0 when there is no previous buffer, and, when a previous block was read (block-aligned position with a block before it), the buffer pointer value converted to int, which is not an errno (a latent bug of the code). No lock besides the folio lock is taken.
note: Reviewer wrong: affs/file.c:832-836 (err_bh: bh = prev_bh; if (!written) written = PTR_ERR(bh); goto done) does assign PTR_ERR of the previous buffer; only the wording of the quirk was made more exact.

name: ceph_set_acl
prose: Precondition: dentry is a valid dentry with a valid inode; acl is NULL (remove the ACL) or a valid posix_acl owned by the caller; type is an ACL type.
