Postcondition: returns -EROFS if the inode is a snapshot inode (ceph_snap != CEPH_NOSNAP) with nothing changed; for type ACL_TYPE_ACCESS with non-NULL acl, posix_acl_update_mode may fail and its error is returned (it may also drop acl to NULL if the ACL is representable by the mode, in which case the xattr is removed); for ACL_TYPE_DEFAULT on a non-directory it returns -EINVAL if acl is non-NULL and 0 if acl is NULL, modifying nothing and caching nothing; for any other type it returns -EINVAL. With a non-NULL acl a buffer is kmalloc'd (-ENOMEM on failure) and the ACL is encoded (a negative return of posix_acl_to_xattr is returned); if the mode changed, __ceph_setattr is called to set mode/ctime and its nonzero error is returned; then __ceph_setxattr sets (or removes, when value is NULL) the ACL xattr: on its failure the old mode and ctime are restored via __ceph_setattr if the mode had been changed, and its error is returned. On full success ceph_set_cached_acl(inode, type, acl) is called under i_ceph_lock and 0 is returned: if the XATTR_SHARED cap is issued it calls set_cached_acl, which stores acl in the inode's ACL cache taking its own additional reference on it (posix_acl_dup) and releasing the previously cached ACL; otherwise it calls forget_cached_acl and nothing is cached, so success does not guarantee the ACL is cached. The temporary xattr buffer is always freed. The caller keeps its own reference on acl, which this function does not drop.
note: Reviewer right: ceph_set_cached_acl (acl.c:20-31) calls set_cached_acl, which does xchg(p, posix_acl_dup(acl)) and releases the old cached value (fs/posix_acl.c:81-89), i.e. a reference is taken by the cache; the old text said no reference is taken.

name: __ceph_setattr
prose: Real function __ceph_setattr(idmap, inode, attr, cia) in fs/ceph/inode.c (the slice is its middle part, so the name is not in the slice; the wrapper ceph_setattr is a different function outside this slice). Precondition: inode is a ceph inode, attr says which attributes to change (ia_valid), cia is NULL or carries an fscrypt_auth buffer owned by the caller, and the caller holds the inode lock. Postcondition: it finds an alias dentry with d_find_alias and, if there is one, builds its path and checks MDS access for MAY_WRITE; if that check returns -EACCES the function returns -EACCES at once with nothing changed; any other failure to build the path or check access, or having no alias, only sets do_sync (no local application under exclusive caps) and continues. It allocates a cap flush (-ENOMEM if that fails) and creates a SETATTR MDS request (its error is returned, after freeing the cap flush, if creation fails). Under i_ceph_lock it reads the issued caps; if the inode has no head snap context and caps include an EXCL cap or FILE_WR it takes mdsc->snap_rwsem for reading (re-reading the caps if i_ceph_lock had to be dropped). If cia->fscrypt_auth is set: when it is larger than the allowed size, or when CONFIG_FS_ENCRYPTION is off, it returns -EINVAL after dropping i_ceph_lock and putting the request and cap flush, without releasing snap_rwsem if it was taken; otherwise it either installs the buffer in the inode (when !do_sync and AUTH_EXCL is issued; the old buffer is freed) or puts it in the request, and in both cases sets cia->fscrypt_auth to NULL (ownership passed). For each of ATTR_UID, GID, MODE, ATIME, SIZE, MTIME and ATTR_CTIME (when no other of the uid, gid, mode, atime, mtime or size flags is set) it either applies the change to the inode locally under the matching EXCL (or, for atime and mtime, a newer value under FILE_WR) cap and records the dirtied caps, or, when the shared cap is not issued or the value differs, puts it into the request mask and the caps to release; a growing size under FILE_EXCL (without do_sync) is applied locally and also marks the mtime for update, and an encrypted inode shrunk to a non-block-aligned size is done by the request with the fscrypt RMW data. If any caps were dirtied it marks them dirty (__ceph_mark_dirty_caps), sets the inode ctime from attr->ia_ctime and increments the inode version. It then restricts the caps to release to those issued, drops i_ceph_lock and snap_rwsem if held, and marks the inode dirty as required. If the request mask is non-zero it gives the request a reference on the inode (ihold) and sends it with ceph_mdsc_do_request (an fscrypt_truncate fill failure is returned as the error instead, without sending); if the MDS answers -EAGAIN and fewer than 20 retries were used it puts the request, frees the cap flush and starts over. At the exit it puts the request, frees the cap flush and, if the result is non-negative and the mask included the size, runs __ceph_do_pending_vmtruncate. It returns 0 on success (including when nothing had to be sent), or the negative errno (the MDS result or one of the errors above).
note: Reviewer right: the slice (inode.c:2590-2841) is the body of __ceph_setattr (head at 2539), not ceph_setattr (2898-2927). The old prose for ceph_setattr was itself accurate for that wrapper (checked) but was not about the code in this record, so it is replaced. The -EINVAL fscrypt_auth path at inode.c:2618-2622 goes to out without up_read(snap_rwsem) (observation of the code, stated in the prose).

name: get_cur_inode_state
prose: Precondition: sctx is a valid send context with sctx->send_root set (sctx->parent_root may be NULL), ino and gen identify an inode, send_gen and parent_gen may be NULL. Postcondition: looks the inode up in the send root (get_inode_info) and then, if sctx->parent_root is non-NULL, in the parent root; an inode absent from a root (-ENOENT) or with nlink 0 there counts as not existing in it. If either lookup fails with a negative errno other than -ENOENT (for example -ENOMEM), that errno is returned unchanged immediately and nothing after that lookup is done. Otherwise, if it exists in both roots, the result is inode_state_no_change when both generations equal gen, inode_state_did_create (ino < sctx->send_progress) or inode_state_will_create when only the send root generation equals gen, inode_state_did_delete or inode_state_will_delete (same test) when only the parent root generation equals gen, and -ENOENT when neither does. If it exists only in the send root, the result is did_create or will_create when its generation equals gen, otherwise -ENOENT; if it exists only in the parent root, did_delete or will_delete when its generation equals gen, otherwise -ENOENT; if in neither, -ENOENT. Side effects: if send_gen is non-NULL it is set, right after the send root lookup succeeded or returned -ENOENT (so before the parent lookup, and it stays set even if the parent lookup then fails with another errno), to the send root generation, or 0 if the inode does not exist there; if parent_gen is non-NULL and sctx->parent_root is non-NULL it is set, only when the parent root lookup did not fail with an errno other than -ENOENT, to the parent root generation, or 0 if the inode does not exist there. send_gen is not written if the send root lookup fails with an errno other than -ENOENT; parent_gen is never written when there is no parent root or when the parent lookup fails with such an errno. No lock, reference or memory is acquired or released by this function itself.
note: Reviewer right: send.c:1818-1840 parent_gen assigned only after the 'ret < 0 && ret != -ENOENT' return; old prose omitted it for the parent lookup. get_inode_info (send.c:910-930) does not write info on -ENOENT, harmless since left_ret/right_ret are then -ENOENT anyway.

name: btrfs_relocate_block_group
prose: Precondition: fs_info is a mounted btrfs filesystem, group_start is the start of a block group and, for a data block group, the caller has started a superblock write section (only checked by ASSERT). Postcondition: it returns early, before taking any reference, with the non-zero result of wait_on_bit on BTRFS_FS_UNFINISHED_DROPS (interrupted wait), -EINTR if the filesystem is closing, or -ENOENT if no block group starts at group_start; after taking the block group reference it returns -ETXTBSY if the block group is pinned by a swapfile or -ENOMEM if the reloc control cannot be allocated (the block group reference is put before these two returns). Otherwise it starts a reloc chunk (reloc_chunk_start; on failure it puts the block group reference, frees the reloc control and returns that error without ending a chunk), sets the block group read-only (btrfs_inc_block_group_ro), looks up the free space cache inode and, if found, deletes the cache with delete_block_group_cache, creates the data relocation inode, waits for block group reservations, nocow writers and ordered roots, calls btrfs_zone_finish (its result is ignored apart from a WARN), and then repeatedly calls relocate_block_group under fs_info->cleaner_mutex. In each iteration a negative result of relocate_block_group is stored in err; if the stage is MOVE_DATA_EXTENTS and a file extent was found it also calls btrfs_wait_ordered_range on the data inode (a non-zero result there overwrites err, so an earlier relocate_block_group error can be replaced by the ordered-range error), invalidates the inode's page cache and moves to UPDATE_DATA_PTRS; if err is negative the loop exits, and it also exits when no extents were found. It returns 0 on success, in which case the block group stays read-only, or err: the errno from reloc_chunk_start, btrfs_inc_block_group_ro, -ENOMEM for the path allocation, lookup_free_space_inode or delete_block_group_cache (any error other than -ENOENT), create_reloc_inode, or, from the loop, relocate_block_group or btrfs_wait_ordered_range (the later of the two within the same iteration). On every return after the reloc control was allocated the block group reference is put and the reloc control is freed; on the paths after reloc_chunk_start succeeded the data inode is released (iput, which ignores NULL) and the reloc chunk is ended (reloc_chunk_end), and on an error after the block group was made read-only the read-only count is dropped again (btrfs_dec_block_group_ro).
note: Reviewer right: relocation.c ~4000-4010 'ret = btrfs_wait_ordered_range(...); if (ret) err = ret;' overwrites err; also lookup_free_space_inode error (PTR_ERR(inode) != -ENOENT) is returned, which old prose omitted.

name: ceph_flush_snaps
prose: Precondition: ci is a valid inode info and the caller holds an inode reference; the caller does NOT hold ci->i_ceph_lock; psession is NULL or points to a session pointer (possibly NULL) whose reference the caller holds. Postcondition: always returns void with ci->i_ceph_lock released. If CEPH_I_FLUSH_SNAPS is not set, or ci has no auth cap, nothing is flushed. Otherwise, if the passed session is for a different MDS than the auth cap's, its reference is dropped and the correct session is looked up (reference taken) under mdsc->mutex and the check repeated; once a session matches, CEPH_I_KICK_FLUSH (if set) causes __kick_flushing_caps first, then __ceph_flush_snaps(ci, session) is invoked. Session reference handling: if psession is non-NULL, *psession is set to the current session (reference transferred back to the caller, possibly NULL or a newly looked up one, even if nothing was flushed); if psession is NULL the session reference is dropped. Finally, under mdsc->snap_flush_lock ci is removed from the snap-flush queue (list_del_init) in every case, and if it was queued the inode reference is released with iput.
note: Verified caps.c:1740-1796: lock taken/released, list_del_init + iput(need_put) on every path, *psession/put exactly as stated. Minor unstated: if the session lookup returns NULL the retry loop repeats (not a false claim).

name: handle_cap_grant
prose: Precondition: handle_cap_grant(inode, session, cap, grant, xattr_buf, extra_info): the caller holds session->s_mutex, ci->i_ceph_lock, and (for a CEPH_CAP_OP_IMPORT grant) session->s_mdsc->snap_rwsem for reading; cap belongs to inode (the auth cap or, for a non-import grant, possibly a non-auth cap), grant is a decoded mds caps message, xattr_buf is the buffer holding the xattr blob (used only if a newer xattr version is accepted), and extra_info holds the decoded ancillary data. Postcondition: returns void; it releases ci->i_ceph_lock and session->s_mutex on return and, if grant->op is IMPORT, also releases snap_rwsem (read). While under the lock: if the cap generation was stale, cap->issued and cap->implemented are reset to CEPH_CAP_PIN; if the message seq is not newer than cap->seq the cap's seq and its issued caps are retained (newcaps |= cap->issued); cap->cap_gen is set to the current session generation and cap->seq to the message seq; mode/uid/gid, nlink, xattr blob (taking a ref on xattr_buf and dropping the old blob when version is newer), times, dir stats, layout (the replaced old pool_ns is returned to the caller through extra_info->pool_ns), file size/truncate state, max_size on the auth cap, and inline version are updated from the grant according to which caps (newcaps) and extra_info->issued allow; cap->issued becomes newcaps (kept within cap->implemented, which only gains bits; BUG_ON otherwise). A revocation of cached or buffered caps may queue writeback or invalidation and set CEPH_I_FLUSH_FORCE when a revoke ack must be deferred; a revoke op otherwise clears cap->mds_wanted and forces a flush ack. After unlocking it may fill inline data, queue vmtruncate/writeback/invalidate, invalidate aliases for a deleted inode (nlink 0), wake ci->i_cap_wq waiters, and finally, after s_mutex has been released, call ceph_check_caps when check_caps was set (auth cap only, or all caps, always with CHECK_CAPS_NOINVAL, plus CHECK_CAPS_FLUSH_FORCE when the op is a revoke whose ack was not deferred).
note: Reviewer wrong: caps.c:3532 comment 'caller holds s_mutex and i_ceph_lock, we drop both', mutex_unlock(&session->s_mutex) ~3866, up_read(&session->s_mdsc->snap_rwsem) in the IMPORT branch ~3843, spin_unlock i_ceph_lock; __releases annotations at 3541. Only tightened the final ceph_check_caps sentence (FLUSH_FORCE only for non-deferred revoke).

name: btrfs_create_pending_block_groups
prose: Precondition: trans is a valid transaction handle whose new_bgs list holds block groups created in this transaction that have not yet been fully inserted into the trees. Postcondition: returns nothing and always empties trans->new_bgs, releasing the list's reference on every block group. For each block group in order: if an earlier block group left a non-zero ret the steps below are skipped; otherwise it inserts the block group item (a failure aborts the transaction), then, if BLOCK_GROUP_FLAG_CHUNK_ITEM_INSERTED is not set, adds the chunk item under fs_info->chunk_mutex (failure aborts the transaction), then inserts the device extents (failure aborts the transaction), then calls btrfs_add_block_group_free_space, and adds the sysfs entry for its raid type if missing. These steps are not skipped by a failure of an earlier step for the same block group (only the result of the last attempted step, insert_dev_extents, carries into the next group). In every case it then drops the delayed-refs reservation for the block group insert, removes the block group from the list under unused_bgs_lock, clears BLOCK_GROUP_FLAG_NEW and puts the list reference; if ret is 0 and the group is still unused it is marked unused (btrfs_mark_bg_unused). Finally it releases the transaction's reserved chunk metadata. Failures are reported only through transaction abort, never through a return value.
note: Reviewer wrong: block-group.c btrfs_create_pending_block_groups: 'btrfs_dec_delayed_refs_rsv_bg_inserts; spin_lock(unused_bgs_lock); list_del_init(&bg_list); clear_bit NEW; btrfs_put_block_group; unlock' at label next, then btrfs_trans_release_chunk_metadata(trans) at the end; steps skipped via 'if (ret) goto next' (ret = last insert_dev_extents result). Prose matches.

name: afs_do_setlk
prose: Precondition: file is an open AFS file whose inode maps to a live afs_vnode, fl is a lock request not yet linked on any vnode list, the caller holds no vnode->lock. Postcondition: initialises fl->fl_ops, the fl_u.afs link and state AFS_LOCK_PENDING (and an unset flock mode is treated as openafs; a partial-file request in write mode is treated as a write lock), then returns, after possibly sleeping, one of the following. A negative errno from afs_do_setlk_check, i.e. from afs_validate or afs_check_permit, or -EACCES if the permit lacks the rights needed for the lock type; nothing is queued in that case. 0 if the lock was granted and registered with the VFS (locks_lock_file_wait succeeded); in that case afs_validate is called once more and its result is ignored; for server-backed locks fl is then on vnode->granted_locks with state AFS_LOCK_GRANTED; for flock mode local, or a partial-file lock in openafs mode, no server lock is taken and fl is not put on any vnode list. -ENOENT if vnode->lock_state is AFS_VNODE_LOCK_DELETED (fl was already added to pending_locks and is left there). -EAGAIN if the request has no FL_SLEEP and, with lock_state NONE, the file is locked by someone else on the server, or the server answers would-block (fl is removed from pending_locks and the next locker is woken); with FL_SLEEP, would-block instead sets lock_state WAITING_FOR_CB, queues lock_work after HZ*5 and waits. If the server RPC fails: permission errors (-EKEYREJECTED, -EKEYEXPIRED, -EKEYREVOKED, -EPERM, -EACCES), -ENOENT or any other error is returned after being stored in fl->fl_u.afs.state, unlinking fl and passing the lock to the next locker (or killing lockers on -ENOENT). A request waits (even one without FL_SLEEP) when vnode->lock_state is not NONE and no instant grant from an existing server lock applies: it sleeps interruptibly until fl state leaves AFS_LOCK_PENDING; a signal returns -ERESTARTSYS with fl left on pending_locks, a state of YOUR_TRY retries the server request, GRANTED completes, and a negative state set by another path is returned as the error. If locks_lock_file_wait fails its negative errno is returned and, for server-backed locks, fl is unlinked from its vnode list and afs_defer_unlock is called, which queues release of the server lock only if no granted locks remain and the lock state is GRANTED or EXTENDING. vnode->lock is not held on return. It may set vnode->lock_key (key reference taken), lock_type and lock_state SETTING/WAITING_FOR_CB.
note: Reviewer partly right: flock.c:~484 afs_do_setlk ends with 'afs_validate(vnode, key);' ignoring its result, while afs_do_setlk_check (flock.c ~384) returns validate errors; old prose was ambiguous. Also fixed: non-blocking requests can wait when lock_state != NONE (~need_to_wait path), afs_defer_unlock only queues unlock if granted_locks empty and state GRANTED/EXTENDING, removed unsupported 'never returns -EINPROGRESS'.

name: DEADLINE_DEBUGFS_DDIR_ATTRS(DD_RT_PRIO, DD_READ, read0)
prose: Generated function deadline_read0_fifo_stop(m, v). Precondition: m->private points to a valid request_queue q whose q->elevator->elevator_data is the mq-deadline struct deadline_data dd, and dd->lock is held, acquired by the matching deadline_read0_fifo_start of the same seq_file iteration; v is ignored. Postcondition: releases dd->lock with spin_unlock and returns nothing; no other state is changed.
note: Verified mq-deadline.c DEADLINE_DEBUGFS_DDIR_ATTRS macro: _fifo_stop reads q = m->private, dd = q->elevator->elevator_data, does spin_unlock(&dd->lock) only. Only tightened the elevator_data path wording.

name: btrfs_commit_transaction
prose: Precondition: trans is the only user of its handle (use_count == 1, only asserted) for a transaction of trans->fs_info and the caller holds no transaction-related lock. Postcondition: in every case the caller's handle is consumed (ended through btrfs_end_transaction, or freed on the commit and cleanup paths), so the caller must not use trans afterwards. The pending snapshot attached to trans (if any) is linked into cur_trans->pending_snapshots by add_pending_snapshot only on two paths: when another task is already committing (see below), and on the committing path just before the state becomes COMMIT_DOING. It is NOT linked on the early exits (transaction already aborted, btrfs_run_delayed_refs or btrfs_start_dirty_block_groups failing) nor on the committing-path failures before that point (previous transaction aborted, -EROFS, delayed items failing). Early exits: if the transaction is already aborted it returns the abort error, and if btrfs_run_delayed_refs(trans, 0) (performed only by the task that sets BTRFS_DELAYED_REFS_FLUSHING) or btrfs_start_dirty_block_groups fails it returns that negative errno; in these cases the handle is ended with btrfs_end_transaction and the transaction is not cleaned up. Before that, btrfs_trans_release_metadata is called and trans->block_rsv is set to NULL (except in the already-aborted case, which exits earlier), and btrfs_create_pending_block_groups is called. If another task is already committing (state at least COMMIT_PREP) the snapshot is linked, a reference is taken on cur_trans, the handle is ended, and it waits until the commit is COMPLETED (SUPER_COMMITTED for an fsync); it returns the transaction's abort error if it aborted, otherwise the result of btrfs_end_transaction. Otherwise this task performs the commit: it sets the state to COMMIT_PREP, waits for the previous transaction if it has not reached the wanted state (if that one aborted, its error is returned via the cleanup path) and, when there is no previous transaction on the list but the filesystem is in an error state, fails with -EROFS (via the cleanup path); then it sets COMMIT_START, flushes delalloc and runs delayed items, waits for extent writers and ordered extents, pauses scrub, links the pending snapshot and sets COMMIT_DOING, waits until it is the only writer, and if the transaction was aborted meanwhile returns the abort error via the cleanup path. It then takes reloc_mutex, creates pending snapshots, runs delayed items and delayed refs, commits fs roots and cow-only roots, accounts qgroups, switches the commit roots, updates the superblock copy, takes tree_log_mutex, sets UNBLOCKED (running_transaction becomes NULL), writes the btree (btrfs_write_and_wait_transaction; a failure there is reported with btrfs_handle_fs_error) and the superblocks, sets SUPER_COMMITTED, finishes the extent commit, sets the last committed transid, sets COMPLETED, removes the transaction from the list, puts two references on it, ends the freezable write section if applicable, resumes scrub, detaches the handle from the task if current and frees the handle, and returns 0. If any step from the delayed-items failure up to finish_extent_commit fails (after the early exits) the commit path jumps to the cleanup: scrub is resumed if it was paused, reserved metadata and pending block groups and chunk metadata are released, a warning is logged, the handle is detached from the task, and cleanup_transaction aborts the transaction with that errno, removes and destroys it and frees the handle; the negative errno is returned.
note: Reviewer right: transaction.c btrfs_commit_transaction: 'goto lockdep_trans_commit_start_release' (aborted / run_delayed_refs / start_dirty_block_groups) returns before any add_pending_snapshot; also failures at prev_trans abort, -EROFS, start_delalloc_flush, run_delayed_items go to lockdep_release/cleanup before the COMMIT_DOING add_pending_snapshot. Old prose also said 'in every case linked' and described cleanup-path errors as direct returns; write_all_supers failure is not reported via btrfs_handle_fs_error.

name: aio_poll_wake
prose: Precondition: wait is the wait-queue entry embedded in the poll_iocb of a live aio_kiocb; the caller holds the waitqueue lock (head->lock); key is the poll key (may be NULL, giving mask 0). Postcondition: returns 0 with no effect if mask is nonzero and shares no bit with req->events. Otherwise returns 1 and does one of: (a) completes inline when mask != 0, req->work_scheduled is false and spin_trylock_irqsave(ctx_lock) succeeds: removes the entry from the waitqueue, removes the iocb from ctx->active_reqs, sets ki_res.res = mangle_poll(mask), and then drops the iocb reference with iocb_put after releasing ctx_lock, except that if an eventfd is attached and eventfd_signal_allowed() is false the put is deferred to a scheduled aio_poll_put_work; or (b) otherwise (mask == 0, work already scheduled or trylock failed): schedules req->work and sets work_scheduled if it was not set, else sets work_need_resched; and if mask has POLLFREE in this branch it also sets req->cancelled, removes the entry from the waitqueue and, as the last step, publishes req->head = NULL with a release store. POLLFREE is not specially handled on the inline path.
note: Verified aio.c aio_poll_wake line by line (mask/events check, trylock inline path incl. eventfd deferral, else-branch scheduling, POLLFREE cancel/list_del_init/smp_store_release as last step).

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE5(io_getevents, aio_context_t, ctx_id,
prose: Generated syscall sys_io_getevents(ctx_id, min_nr, nr, events, timeout) (CONFIG_64BIT). Precondition: events is a user buffer for up to nr struct io_event; timeout, if non-NULL, points to a user struct __kernel_timespec giving a relative timeout. Postcondition: returns -EFAULT if timeout is non-NULL and get_timespec64 fails (it fails only when the copy from user faults). Otherwise it calls do_io_getevents (timeout NULL means wait indefinitely, KTIME_MAX): that returns -EINVAL if ctx_id does not name a context, or if min_nr < 0 or min_nr > nr, and otherwise the result of read_events: the number of events copied to the user buffer (0 or fewer than min_nr if the timeout expired or a signal interrupted the wait; a timeout or interrupted wait does not itself produce an error from read_events), or a negative errno (-EFAULT if copying to the user buffer faulted, -EINVAL if the context is dead) which is returned only when no event had been copied yet. The result is stored in an int; if it is 0 and a signal is pending it is replaced by -EINTR. The context reference taken by do_io_getevents is dropped. The ring head is advanced past the events copied by each successful ring read; a faulting copy leaves that read's events unconsumed.
note: Corrected: aio.c read_events (1312-1367) breaks out on ret2 (-ETIME/-ERESTARTSYS) but returns ret (count), so an interrupted wait is not a negative errno from read_events; errors from aio_read_events (1294-1305) are stored in *i only if *i == 0. get_timespec64 (time.c:872) fails only with -EFAULT.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE6(io_pgetevents_time32
prose: Generated syscall sys_io_pgetevents_time32(ctx_id, min_nr, nr, events, timeout, usig), compiled only for 32-bit with CONFIG_COMPAT_32BIT_TIME. Precondition: timeout, if non-NULL, points to a user struct old_timespec32 (relative); usig, if non-NULL, points to a user struct __aio_sigset. Postcondition: returns -EFAULT if the timeout or the sigset cannot be copied from user; returns the non-zero error of set_user_sigmask (e.g. -EINVAL for a bad sigsetsize) before waiting; otherwise waits for events with do_io_getevents (number of events read, -EINVAL for a bad context or min_nr outside 0..nr, or a read_events error), restores the saved signal mask unless a signal is pending (restore_saved_sigmask_unless), and returns -ERESTARTNOHAND if a signal is pending and the result is 0, else the result.
note: Verified aio.c 2292-2445 io_pgetevents_time32: get_old_timespec32/copy_from_user -> -EFAULT, set_user_sigmask error returned before waiting, do_io_getevents, restore_saved_sigmask_unless(interrupted), -ERESTARTNOHAND if interrupted && !ret.

name: COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE6(io_pgetevents,
prose: Generated compat syscall compat_sys_io_pgetevents(ctx_id, min_nr, nr, events, timeout, usig) (CONFIG_COMPAT_32BIT_TIME). Precondition: timeout, if non-NULL, points to a user struct old_timespec32; usig, if non-NULL, points to a user struct __compat_aio_sigset. Postcondition: returns -EFAULT if the timeout or the sigset cannot be copied from user; returns the non-zero error of set_compat_user_sigmask(compat_ptr(ksig.sigmask), ksig.sigsetsize) (e.g. -EINVAL) before waiting; otherwise waits with do_io_getevents (events read, -EINVAL for a bad context or min_nr outside 0..nr, or a read_events error), restores the saved signal mask unless a signal is pending, and returns -ERESTARTNOHAND if a signal is pending and the result is 0, else the result.
note: Verified aio.c 2292-2445 COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE6(io_pgetevents): same structure with get_old_timespec32 and set_compat_user_sigmask(compat_ptr(ksig.sigmask), ksig.sigsetsize).

name: exfat_get_cluster
prose: Real function exfat_get_cluster(inode, cluster, fclus, dclus, last_dclus, allow_eof) (the packet name exfat_find_last_cluster does not exist in the source and the slice cuts the function head). Precondition: inode is a valid exfat inode, cluster is the file-relative cluster index to locate, fclus, dclus and last_dclus point to writable unsigned ints, and allow_eof is non-zero if reaching the end of the chain at or before cluster is acceptable; the caller holds the filesystem lock as usual for exfat chain walks. Postcondition: returns 0 or -EIO. If ei->start_clu is EXFAT_FREE_CLUSTER it reports a filesystem error and returns -EIO with the output variables untouched. Otherwise it sets *fclus = 0 and *dclus = *last_dclus = ei->start_clu; if cluster == 0 or ei->start_clu == EXFAT_EOF_CLUSTER it returns 0 without using the cache. Otherwise it looks up the nearest cached position with exfat_cache_lookup (updating *fclus/*dclus), returns 0 at once (without exfat_cache_add) if *fclus == cluster, and else walks the FAT chain with exfat_ent_get, updating *last_dclus to the previous cluster, *dclus to the next one and incrementing *fclus per step. It returns -EIO when *fclus exceeds the filesystem's cluster count (chain loop, reported as a fs error), when exfat_ent_get fails, or when the chain reaches EXFAT_EOF_CLUSTER and allow_eof is zero (reported as a fs error), in each case without calling exfat_cache_add and leaving the outputs at the partial-walk values. On success it records the traversed run with exfat_cache_add and returns 0 with *fclus == cluster and *dclus the cluster's number and *last_dclus the preceding cluster's number, or (allow_eof) with *dclus == EXFAT_EOF_CLUSTER, *last_dclus the last valid cluster and *fclus <= cluster.
note: Reviewer wrong: the EXFAT_FREE_CLUSTER check is in the head cut from the slice: fs/exfat/cache.c:~248 'if (ei->start_clu == EXFAT_FREE_CLUSTER) { exfat_fs_error(...); return -EIO; }' (function exfat_get_cluster starts at the line before). Rest of prose re-verified against cache.c:262-309.

name: cow_file_range
prose: Precondition: inode is a btrfs inode, [start, end] is a delalloc range whose data space is reserved and whose extent bits are locked by the caller, locked_folio is NULL or the locked folio covering the start of the range, done_offset is NULL or a valid pointer, flags is a combination of COW_FILE_RANGE_* flags, and the range length (aligned to sectorsize, at least one sector) does not exceed the filesystem total bytes (only asserted). Postcondition: for a free-space inode it returns -EINVAL after the error cleanup below (nothing was reserved, so only the delalloc/lock bits of the whole range are cleared and the data reservation released). Unless COW_FILE_RANGE_NO_INLINE is set it first calls cow_file_range_inline: a result of 0 is returned as 1 (the range was written inline and the IO and cleanup are already done), a negative result is returned unchanged (cow_file_range_inline has already cleaned up), both jumping to done, which sets *done_offset = end when done_offset is non-NULL and returns; a positive result (inline not possible) continues with the normal path. Otherwise it loops, reserving an extent with btrfs_reserve_extent (exact size, at least min_alloc_size), and for each reserved extent locks that extent range, creates the io extent map and an ordered extent, (for the data relocation root clones csums into the ordered extent with btrfs_reloc_clone_csums), advancing start; on the zoned -EAGAIN case it waits for a zone to finish and retries when still at the original start, otherwise with done_offset non-NULL it shortens end to start - 1 and ends the loop with 0, and with done_offset NULL it fails with -ENOSPC. After the loop it clears LOCKED and DELALLOC over [orig_start, end], applies PAGE_UNLOCK (unless COW_FILE_RANGE_KEEP_LOCKED) and PAGE_SET_ORDERED to the folios, and returns 0 through done (setting *done_offset = end if done_offset is non-NULL). On a failure after the setup the function returns the negative errno after the error cleanup (it logs an error with btrfs_err, never writes *done_offset, and calls mapping_set_error on the inode mapping when some part before start was already processed and locked_folio is NULL). The cleanup depends on where it failed: (a) btrfs_reserve_extent fails (other than the handled -EAGAIN) or -ENOSPC from -EAGAIN: nothing to undo for the current extent; (b) btrfs_create_io_em fails: the extent range is unlocked, the block group reservation is dropped and the reserved extent is freed; (c) btrfs_alloc_ordered_extent fails: the range is unlocked, the extent map range is dropped, then as (b); (d) btrfs_reloc_clone_csums fails: the extent map range is dropped, the ordered extent reference is put and the block group reservation is dropped, start is advanced past this extent, but the reserved extent is NOT freed here (it belongs to the ordered extent, whose cleanup is part of cleaning up [orig_start, start)). In all failure cases it then cleans up the ordered extents for [orig_start, start) and clears LOCKED and DELALLOC and ends writeback on those folios, for the current extent (cases b and c) clears the bits, unlocks the folios and frees its data qgroup reservation, and for the untouched rest (when start + cur_alloc_size < end) also clears the bits including the data reservation, unlocks the folios and frees its data qgroup reservation.
note: Reviewer right: inode.c cow_file_range ~1415-1432: on btrfs_reloc_clone_csums failure only btrfs_drop_extent_map_range, put ordered, btrfs_dec_block_group_reservations, start advanced, cur_alloc_size = 0 -> goto out_unlock; btrfs_free_reserved_extent is only at out_reserve (create_io_em / alloc_ordered_extent failures). Also added positive-return-of-cow_file_range_inline fall-through and per-failure cleanup differences.

name: btrfs_do_encoded_write
prose: Precondition: iocb and from describe a write to a btrfs inode, encoded is a valid btrfs_ioctl_encoded_io_args, and the caller owns iocb, from and encoded. Postcondition: returns -EINVAL, with nothing allocated and ki_pos unchanged, if the compression type is not ZLIB, ZSTD or an LZO size matching the filesystem sector size, if encryption is not NONE, the inode is NODATASUM, unencoded_len exceeds BTRFS_MAX_UNCOMPRESSED, the byte count remaining in from (orig_count) is 0, exceeds BTRFS_MAX_COMPRESSED or is not smaller than unencoded_len, or if the start (iocb->ki_pos), the end (only when start + encoded->len is below i_size) or unencoded_offset is not sector aligned. Then it allocates and fills a folio array with the compressed data from from, zero-padded to a sector multiple (-ENOMEM or -EFAULT on failure, freeing all folios), loops waiting for ordered extents (btrfs_wait_ordered_range) and invalidating the page cache (invalidate_inode_pages2_range) and locking the extent range until no ordered extent or page remains in it, then reserves data chunk space, qgroup data and delalloc metadata. It tries an inline extent only when unencoded_len == encoded->len, unencoded_offset == 0 and can_cow_file_range_inline(inode, start, encoded->len, orig_count) is true; if __cow_file_range_inline returns 0 the result is orig_count and the function goes to the release path below, if it returns a negative errno that errno is the failure result, and if it returns a positive value (or the inline test was false) the normal path follows: it reserves a disk extent (btrfs_reserve_extent), creates the io extent map and an ordered extent flagged ENCODED and COMPRESSED, extends i_size if the write passes it, unlocks the range, releases the delalloc extents and submits the compressed write (the folios are then owned by that IO and not freed here). On success (both paths) it returns the byte count orig_count (positive) and advances iocb->ki_pos by encoded->len; on the inline path the folios are put and freed here, delalloc extents and metadata are released and the extent range is unlocked. On failure it returns the negative errno from btrfs_wait_ordered_range, invalidate_inode_pages2_range, btrfs_alloc_data_chunk_ondemand, btrfs_qgroup_reserve_data, btrfs_delalloc_reserve_metadata, __cow_file_range_inline, btrfs_reserve_extent, btrfs_create_io_em or btrfs_alloc_ordered_extent, with ki_pos unchanged, the extent range unlocked if it was locked, the reserved extent freed and the block group reservation dropped (and the extent map range dropped when the ordered extent allocation failed) when an extent had been reserved, the delalloc, qgroup and data space reservations made so far released, and all folios put and the array freed.
note: Reviewer right: inode.c ~9962-9965 inline attempt condition is 'unencoded_len == len && unencoded_offset == 0 && can_cow_file_range_inline(...)'; old prose omitted the helper (and positive __cow_file_range_inline falls through). Rest re-verified against 9817-10067 (error labels out_free_reserved/out_delalloc_release/out_qgroup_free_data/out_free_data_space/out_unlock/out_folios).

name: btrfs_recover_log_trees
prose: Precondition: called during mount with log_root_tree the log root tree of the filesystem, on a filesystem being mounted read-write, with no other log replay in progress. Postcondition: returns -ENOMEM at once if the path cannot be allocated. Otherwise it sets BTRFS_FS_LOG_RECOVERING, starts a transaction on the tree root (a failure is returned after cleanup), pins all blocks of the log root tree, and then walks all log roots (TREE_LOG_OBJECTID root items, from the highest offset downward) in the stages pin, replay inodes, and replay everything: for each log root it reads the log tree and looks up the subvolume root with the same id; if the subvolume root does not exist (-ENOENT) the log's root block is pinned and the log is skipped; otherwise the log root is attached to the subvolume root, the root is recorded in the transaction, the log tree is walked, and in the final stage the inode link counts are fixed up and the root's free objectid is re-initialised. Temporary root references (the log root and the subvolume root) are dropped for each log. After the last stage the path is freed, the transaction is committed (which unpins the blocks) and, if the commit succeeded, BTRFS_FS_LOG_RECOVERING is cleared and 0 is returned; if the commit fails its error is returned and the flag stays set. On any error before the commit (walk_log_tree, btrfs_search_slot, btrfs_read_tree_root, btrfs_get_fs_root other than -ENOENT, btrfs_pin_extent_for_log_replay, btrfs_record_root_in_trans, fixup_inode_link_counts, btrfs_init_root_free_objectid) the transaction is aborted (not when starting it failed), the transaction handle is ended if one was started, the log root reference is put, BTRFS_FS_LOG_RECOVERING is cleared, the path is freed and the negative errno is returned.
note: Verified tree-log.c btrfs_recover_log_trees (alloc path, set LOG_RECOVERING, start trans, pin walk, per-log loop with ENOENT skip + pin, fixup/init_root_free_objectid at REPLAY_ALL, next: label puts root/log, commit then clear flag only on success, error: label ends wc.trans, puts wc.log, clears flag, frees path).

name: bm_entry_write
prose: Precondition: file is an open binfmt_misc entry file whose inode->i_private is its Node e; buffer is a user pointer to count readable bytes. Postcondition: parses the command with parse_command. If that returns 1 ('0') it clears the entry's Enabled bit; 2 ('1') sets the Enabled bit; 3 ('-1') takes the root inode lock (inode_lock_nested, I_MUTEX_PARENT), and if the entry is still on the entries list removes it (remove_binfmt_handler: unlinks it under misc->entries_lock and removes its dentry), then releases the root inode lock. In these three cases it returns count (the number of bytes consumed, not the parse_command code). Otherwise (parse_command returned 0 for count == 0, -EINVAL for count > 3 or an unknown command, or -EFAULT if copy_from_user failed) it returns that value unchanged and does nothing else. *ppos is not used or advanced and no reference is taken; the root inode lock is not held on return.
note: Reviewer right: binfmt_misc.c parse_command: 'if (count > 3) return -EINVAL;' before any copy; so count at most 3 is not a precondition, count > 3 is a defined -EINVAL result (bm_entry_write default: return res). Prose already listed -EINVAL for count > 3, contradicting the precondition.

name: afs_select_vlserver
prose: Precondition: vc was initialised by afs_begin_vlserver_operation (nr_iterations starts at -1); on calls after the first, vc->call_error and vc->call_abort_code hold the outcome of the previous call and vc->alist and vc->server_list hold the references acquired by earlier calls; single-threaded per cursor. Postcondition: always increments vc->nr_iterations first. Then, if AFS_VL_CURSOR_STOP is already set, it returns false with nothing else changed. On the first call (nr_iterations == 0) it starts iteration (afs_start_vl_iteration: may wait for a DNS lookup; errors -ERESTARTSYS, -ENOENT, -EDESTADDRREQ recorded in cumul_error; an empty server list returns false without setting an error and leaves the server_list reference held) and sends probes (an error is recorded in cumul_error). A failure in either step ends as a failure return (see below). On later calls it first writes call_error to the used address's last_error and evaluates it: error 0 or any error not listed below: cumul_error.error = error, sets STOP and returns false, leaving the vc->alist and vc->server_list references for afs_end_vlserver_operation to release; -ECONNABORTED with abort code AFSVL_IO, AFSVL_BADVOLOPER or AFSVL_NOMEM records -EREMOTEIO and moves to the next server, any other abort code is recorded (afs_prioritise_error) and the cursor fails; connection errors (-ERFKILL, -EADDRNOTAVAIL, -ENETUNREACH, -EHOSTUNREACH, -EHOSTDOWN, -ECONNREFUSED, -ETIMEDOUT, -ETIME) are recorded and the next untried responding address of the same server is tried (or, if none remains, the next server); -ECONNRESET is recorded, sets AFS_VL_CURSOR_RETRY and goes to the next server; -EOPNOTSUPP goes to the next server without recording an error. Moving to the next server first updates alist->preferred if the last call responded on a different address whose preferred address was tried, and drops the alist reference. Server choice waits for probes (an error from afs_wait_for_vl_probes is recorded and the cursor fails), then picks the preferred server if untried, else the untried responding server with the lowest probe rtt (the last one among equals); if none is left it restarts once from the beginning when RETRY is set (dropping the old alist and server_list references; a second restart fails without recording more) or, when RETRY is not set, records the probe errors of all servers and fails. Returns true when an address has been selected: vc->server, vc->server_index and vc->alist (a reference to the server's address list) are set, vc->addr_index is an address that responded, has not failed its probe and is not yet tried (the preferred one if available), that bit is set in vc->addr_tried and vc->call_responded is false. A false return after a failure also sets AFS_VL_CURSOR_STOP and drops the vc->alist reference if one is held (updating alist->preferred as above), leaves the vc->server_list reference held for afs_end_vlserver_operation (it is NULL only after a restart dropped it), and the final error is in vc->cumul_error.
note: Reviewer right on the contradiction: vl_rotate.c afs_select_vlserver does 'vc->nr_iterations++' before 'if (vc->flags & AFS_VL_CURSOR_STOP) return false'. Also tightened: addr selection excludes probe_failed addresses (iterate_address), server_list may be NULL after a restart, connection errors fall to next server when no address left.

name: ceph_fill_trace
prose: Real function (not a non-function): ceph_fill_trace(sb, req) fills the VFS state (parent directory inode, target inode, dentry and dentry lease) from the parsed MDS reply req->r_reply_info; the slice head is cut so the name is not in the slice. Precondition: req holds a parsed reply (rinfo) with r_session set; the caller (handle_reply) has set req->r_target_inode when rinfo->head->is_target; for the dentry paths req->r_parent, r_dentry and r_old_dentry(_dir) are consistent with the reply and the PARENT_LOCKED flag says whether the parent is locked; the caller holds mdsc->snap_rwsem as ceph_fill_inode requires. Postcondition: returns 0 on success or a negative errno. If the reply has neither a target nor a dentry it returns 0, first calling ceph_invalidate_dir_request when the result is 0 and req->r_parent is set. If is_dentry: the reply directory is looked up with ceph_get_reply_dir (its error is returned) and filled via ceph_fill_inode (its error returned); for a LOOKUPNAME on a locked parent that is not aborted a dentry for the (decrypted) name is found or allocated and stored in req->r_dentry (-ENOMEM, or the filename buffer/decrypt error, on failure). If is_target: ceph_fill_inode is applied to req->r_target_inode (fmode only if not aborted, not async and result 0); on error it sets req->r_target_inode to NULL, discards the inode (discard_new_inode if I_NEW, else iput) and returns that error; on success a new inode is unlocked. Then, depending on flags, dentry and lease handling runs: a null reply dentry deletes a positive dentry or adds a negative one and updates the lease; a target attaches the inode (splice_dentry error returned, -EINVAL if there is no target inode in hand), handles renames by d_move, d_invalidates a mismatched inode, and updates the dentry lease; LOOKUPSNAP/MKSNAP on a locked parent splices the snapdir dentry (error returned); otherwise the lease is updated carefully on an unlocked parent. On exit any extra reference on parent_dir obtained from ceph_get_reply_dir (when it differs from req->r_parent) is dropped with iput; on a failure the target inode is released here only when the ceph_fill_inode call for the target itself fails (req->r_target_inode is then NULL); on any other error return (reply dir, dentry allocation or name decrypt failure before the target is filled, or a splice_dentry failure afterwards) the reference held through req->r_target_inode is NOT dropped by this function, the extra ihold reference taken just before splice_dentry is consumed by d_splice_alias (also on its error), and earlier state changes (parent inode and target inode already filled, req->r_dentry already set, dentry unhashed or invalidated) are not rolled back.
note: Reviewer right: ceph/inode.c ceph_fill_trace: only the 'err = ceph_fill_inode(in, ...)' failure does 'req->r_target_inode = NULL; discard_new_inode/iput'; splice_dentry failures 'goto done' without releasing r_target_inode (ihold ref consumed by d_splice_alias, dcache.c d_splice_alias_ops iput(inode) on all paths). Old closing sentence claimed release on all error paths.
